5Ch5 CPU SchedulingCPU 排程

📌 考試範圍提示：Ch5 係分數最重嘅一章（S26：27/100；F19：40/100；F20：27+；Sp21：26）。必考：

  1. Gantt chart + average waiting / turnaround / response time：FCFS、SJF、SRTF、RR、Priority（± RR）、MLFQ（每年都有！）、自創 policy（LUF、dynamic priority）
  2. RM / EDF real-time Gantt + missed deadlines
  3. MC / short：preemptive vs non-preemptive、convoy effect、starvation & aging、MLFQ 優點、RR vs FCFS、exponential averaging、Little's formula、PCS vs SCS、processor affinity、load balancing、hard vs soft real-time ⚠️ Response time 本科定義 = 第一次運行「完結」時間 − arrival time（slide 5.12），唔係課本「第一次開始」！

1. Basic Concepts（基本概念）[5.4–5.7]

1.1 CPU–I/O Burst Cycle

  • Objective of multiprogramming：have a process running at all times → maximize CPU utilization.
  • Process execution consists of cycles of CPU execution and I/O wait — CPU burst and I/O burst.
  • [5.5] Histogram of CPU-burst times：many short CPU bursts, few long ones (long-tail distribution)。I/O-bound → many short CPU bursts；CPU-bound → a few long CPU bursts. 呢個分佈對設計 scheduling algorithm 好重要。
  • CPU idle 時，OS 由 ready queue 揀一個 process（除非 ready queue empty）→ 由 CPU scheduler（process scheduler / short-term scheduler） 揀。

1.2 When does scheduling happen? ⭐⭐ [5.6]

CPU scheduling 可能喺四種情況發生：

  1. Running → waiting（e.g. I/O request, wait()）
  2. Process terminates
  3. Running → ready（e.g. interrupt / timer）
  4. Waiting → ready（I/O completion）或者 new → ready（新 process 到達，priority 更高）
  • Scheduling under 1 and 2 is non-preemptive (cooperative) — process gives up the CPU voluntarily。
  • Scheduling under 3 and 4 is preemptive.
  • Preemptive 要考慮：access to shared data (race condition, Ch6)、preemption while in kernel mode、interrupts during crucial OS activities。

📝 Sp21 MC：CPU scheduling decisions may take place in → all of the above（running→waiting、terminates、running→ready）。 📝 HW2 MC5：preemptive 例子 → time quantum expires, running process moved back to the ready queue（A terminate、B I/O、D wait() 都係自願 → non-preemptive）。

1.3 Dispatcher [5.7]

  • Dispatcher module gives control of the CPU to the process selected by the CPU scheduler：
    1. switching context from one process to another
    2. switching to user mode
    3. jumping to the proper location in the user program to restart it
  • Dispatch latency — time for the dispatcher to stop one process and start another（overhead）。 應該越快越好。
  • vmstat（Linux）可睇 context switches 數目（每秒幾百次）。

2. Scheduling Metrics（排程指標）⭐⭐⭐ [5.8, 5.12]

Metric 定義 目標
CPU utilization fraction of the time that the CPU is busy max
Throughput number of processes completed per unit time（favors short processes） max
Turnaround time (TAT) time to execute a particular process = completion time − arrival time min
Waiting time (WT) total time spent waiting in the ready queue = TAT − CPU burst min
Response time (RT) time from submission until the first response is produced min
Fairness adequate allocation for different jobs/processes —

2.1 公式（本科 convention，必背）⭐

🧮 Metrics（本科 convention）

TurnaroundWaitingResponse​=Completion−Arrival=Turnaround−CPU burst=(end of the FIRST run)−Arrival​
  • Response time 嘅「first run」完結 = 第一次上 CPU 嘅嗰段（RR / MLFQ 就係 end of first quantum，或者 burst 細過 quantum 就係完成時間）[5.12]。
    • Slide 5.13 例：RR q=4，P1(24), P2(3), P3(3) 全部 t=0 到 → RT：P1 = 4, P2 = 7, P3 = 10，avg = 7。
    • S26 MLFQ 官方：P1 response = 4 − 0 = 4（P1 跑 0–4）。
    • 非 preemptive (FCFS/SJF) 嘅 RT = TAT（第一次 run 就跑完）。
  • Waiting time 另一個計法（gap method）：將 Gantt chart 上 process 唔喺 CPU 嘅時間（由 arrival 起）加埋。兩個方法結果一樣：
    • S26 P2：gap = (4−2)+(21−8)+(40−29)+(57−45)+(64−58) = 44 ✔；formula = 71 − 2 − 25 = 44 ✔。
  • S26 MC19 ✔「Response time is the amount of time from when a request is submitted until the first response is produced」。✗ WT = arrival 到完成（嗰個係 TAT）；✗ TAT = 等 ready queue 時間（嗰個係 WT）；✗ throughput = CPU busy fraction（嗰個係 utilization）。

3. FCFS — First-Come, First-Served ⭐ [5.9–5.10]

  • 按 arrival order 排；non-preemptive（跑完 current CPU burst 先放）。
  • 例：P1 = 24, P2 = 3, P3 = 3（全部 t=0）
    • 次序 P1, P2, P3：0 P1 24 P2 27 P3 30 → WT = 0, 24, 27 → avg 17；TAT avg =324+27+30​=27
    • 次序 P2, P3, P1：0 P2 3 P3 6 P1 30 → WT = 6, 0, 3 → avg 3；TAT avg = 13
  • ⭐ Convoy effect — short processes stuck behind a long process，令 average waiting time 好長，完全取決於 arrival order。One CPU-bound + many I/O-bound → low I/O device utilization。（例：銀行排隊存張支票，前面有人開戶）

📝 HW2 MC6：convoy effect → several short processes wait behind a long process that arrived first。 📝 F19 Q3.2：FCFS 問題 = convoy effect（short process stuck behind a long process）。

4. RR — Round Robin ⭐⭐⭐ [5.11–5.16]

  • FCFS + preemption：每個 process 得 time quantum q（通常 10–100 ms）；用完 → preempted and added to the end (tail) of the ready queue。
  • n processes → each gets 1/n of CPU time in chunks of at most q；no process waits more than (n − 1)q time units ⭐（ignoring context switch）。
  • Timer interrupts every quantum；如果 burst（或 remaining）< q，process 自己完成就放 CPU。
  • 例 [5.13]：q = 4，P1 24, P2 3, P3 3 → 0 P1 4 P2 7 P3 10 P1 14 P1 18 P1 22 P1 26 P1 30
    • WT：P1 = 6, P2 = 4, P3 = 7 → avg 5.67；TAT avg =330+7+10​=15.67；RT = 4, 7, 10 → avg 7
  • RR：average waiting time can be long, but more "fair"；better for short jobs than FCFS；better average response time → good for interactive jobs.

4.1 Time quantum 大細 [5.14, 5.16] ⭐

  • q large → RR degenerates to FCFS.（Sp21 MC 答案：FCFS）
  • q small → many context switches; q must be large w.r.t. context-switch time (< 10 µs), otherwise overhead too high.（q 極細 = processor sharing：好似 n 個 processor 每個 1/n 速度）
  • Average turnaround time does not necessarily improve as q increases.
  • TAT improves if most processes finish their CPU burst within a single quantum.
  • Rule of thumb：80% of CPU bursts should be shorter than q.

4.2 FCFS vs RR ⭐（F19 Q3.2 考過）[5.15]

  • Is RR always better than FCFS? No! 例：10 jobs start at the same time, each needs 100 s, q = 1 s → average turnaround time much worse under RR（全部差唔多 1000 s 先完；FCFS 平均 550 s），but average response time much better。
  • 一般而言 no clear winner between FCFS and RR in TAT/WT — 取決於 burst times、arrival pattern、quantum size。

📝 F19 Q3.2 Model answer：RR performs worse than FCFS in turnaround time when all processes have the same (equal) CPU burst times that are longer than the time quantum — the jobs are interleaved and all finish near the end, whereas FCFS finishes them one by one.

4.3 RR 做 Gantt chart 規則（考試用）

  1. 用 queue（寫低每個時刻 queue 內容！）。
  2. 新到達 process 加入 queue tail；quantum 用完嘅 process 都去 tail。
  3. ⚠️ 同一時刻「新 process 到達」同「running process quantum 用完」→ convention：新到達嗰個先入 queue，然後先放被 preempt 嗰個（寫低 assumption）。
  4. Process burst 完 → 即刻揀下一個（唔使等 quantum 完）。
  5. Queue 空而 running process quantum 用完 → 佢繼續跑（再得一個 quantum）。

5. SJF / SRTF — Shortest Job First ⭐⭐⭐ [5.17–5.24]

5.1 SJF（non-preemptive）

  • Associate each process with the length of its next CPU burst; schedule the shortest.（更準確叫 shortest-next-CPU-burst）
  • ⭐ SJF is optimal — gives the minimum average waiting time for a given set of processes.
  • Difficulty：knowing the length of the next CPU request.（所以 practical 難 implement；F20 MC15 答案 SJF difficult to implement）
  • Sketch proof：moving a short process before a long one decreases the waiting time of the short process more than it increases the waiting time of the long process → average waiting time decreases.
  • 例 [5.18]：P1 = 6, P2 = 8, P3 = 7, P4 = 3。Slide 個 chart 當全部 t = 0 到：0 P4 3 P1 9 P3 16 P2 24 → avg WT =43+16+9+0​=7（slide 答案）。
    • ⚠️ 如果真係跟表入面 arrival（0, 2, 4, 5）：t=0 只有 P1 → 0 P1 6 P4 9 P3 16 P2 24 → WT = 0, 14, 5, 1 → avg 5。考試一定要睇清楚有冇 arrival time。

5.2 SRTF — Shortest-Remaining-Time-First（preemptive SJF）⭐

  • New arrival with burst shorter than the remaining time of the running process → preempts it.
  • Scheduling 喺 every arrival (condition 4) 都要 invoke。
  • 例 [5.23]：P1(0,8), P2(1,4), P3(2,9), P4(3,5) → 0 P1 1 P2 5 P4 10 P1 17 P3 26
    • avg WT =4(10−1)+(1−1)+(17−2)+(5−3)​=426​=6.5

5.3 比較 [5.24] ⭐

  • SJF/SRTF are the best for minimizing average waiting time (and average turnaround time).
  • Provably optimal：SJF among non-preemptive, SRTF among preemptive. SRTF is always at least as good as SJF.
  • SJF/SRTF = FCFS if all processes have the same CPU burst.
  • Can lead to starvation of long processes if shorter processes keep arriving；fairness cannot be enforced.
  • F20 MC14：best (min) average waiting time → SJF（SRTF 亦接受）。

5.4 Exponential Averaging（預測下一個 CPU burst）⭐⭐ [5.19–5.22]

🧮 Exponential averaging

τn+1​=αtn​+(1−α)τn​,0≤α≤1
  • tn​ = actual length of the n-th CPU burst；τn+1​ = predicted value for the next burst；通常 α=1/2。
  • α=0⇒τn+1​=τn​（recent history does not count）；α=1⇒τn+1​=tn​（only the last burst counts）。
  • 展開 → all past values count but recent ones weigh more；past effect diminishes exponentially：
τn+1​=αtn​+(1−α)αtn−1​+⋯+(1−α)jαtn−j​+⋯+(1−α)n+1τ0​
  • 例：α=0.5，10 rounds 後 (1/2)10=1/1024 → 可忽略。
  • 預測取決於 (1) all previous actual bursts with different weights, (2) the initial estimate τ0​。
  • Slide 5.20 例（α=1/2, τ0​=10）：
i 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7
CPU burst ti​ 6 4 6 4 13 13 13 …
guess τi​ 10 8 6 6 5 9 11 12
  • HW2 MC9：τn​=10, tn​=6, α=0.25⇒τn+1​=0.25×6+0.75×10=1.5+7.5= 9 ms。

6. Priority Scheduling ⭐⭐ [5.25–5.27]

  • Each process has a priority number；CPU allocated to the highest priority（本科：smallest integer = highest priority，除非題目另講）。
  • Preemptive（higher-priority arrival preempts）或 non-preemptive。
  • Equal priority → FCFS order（或者 RR）。
  • SJF is a special case of priority scheduling where priority = inverse of predicted next CPU burst.
  • ⭐ Problem：Starvation (indefinite blocking) — low-priority processes may never execute.
  • ⭐ Solution：Aging — gradually increase the priority of a process as it waits（需要每個 process 喺 ready queue 有 timer）。
  • Sp21 MC：main problem of priority scheduling → some processes may never execute (starvation)；HW2 MC7：aging → address starvation by gradually increasing the priority of a waiting process。
  • 例 [5.26]（all t=0；P1 10/3, P2 1/1, P3 2/4, P4 1/5, P5 5/2）→ 0 P2 1 P5 6 P1 16 P3 18 P4 19，avg WT =56+0+16+18+1​=8.2
  • Priority + RR [5.27]：run the highest priority；same priority → round-robin。例 q = 2（burst/priority：P1 4/3, P2 5/2, P3 8/2, P4 7/1, P5 3/3，全部 t=0）→ 0 P4 7 P2 9 P3 11 P2 13 P3 15 P2 16 P3 20 P1 22 P5 24 P1 26 P5 27
    • P4（priority 1）先跑完；P2、P3（priority 2）RR；P2 喺 16 完咗之後 P3 獨自跑到 20；最後 P1、P5（priority 3）RR。

⚠️ Priority + RR 有唔同 arrival time（Lab 5：HW / exam 常見）：被高 priority 新 process preempt 嘅 process 要保留佢剩餘嘅 quantum，唔好 reset（lab 話呢個係 common mistake）。規則同 MLFQ 一樣。

  • Spring 2023 midterm 官方 Gantt（q = 2）：0 P1 1 P2 4 P1 5 P3 7 P1 8 P4 10 P1 11 P3 13 P5 15 P1 16 P3 18 P5 20 P3 22 P5 24 — P1 喺 0–1 被 P2 preempt，4–5 只跑剩低嘅 1 unit 就輪到 P3；8–10 P4 preempt 後 P1 10–11 又用返剩低 1 unit。（由 Gantt 推返嘅 table：P1 (0, 5, pr 2)、P2 (1, 3, pr 1)、P3 (2, 8, pr 2)、P4 (8, 2, pr 1)、P5 (9, 6, pr 2)，模擬器重現完全一致 ✔）

7. Multilevel Queue（多級佇列）⭐ [5.28–5.29]

  • Priority scheduling combined with RR；priority assigned statically；a process remains in the same queue for its whole runtime.
  • Partition processes into queues based on process type（例：real-time → system → interactive → batch）。
  • Each queue can have its own scheduling algorithm.
  • Scheduling among queues：(1) fixed-priority preemptive scheduling（高 queue 空先輪到低 queue → 可能 starvation）或 (2) time-slice（each queue gets a certain % of CPU time，e.g. 60%, 20%, 10%, 10%）。
  • Sp21 MC：Multilevel queue（固定）有 starvation（free from starvation 嘅只有 FCFS 同 RR）。

8. MLFQ — Multilevel Feedback Queue ⭐⭐⭐（每年必考 Gantt）[5.30–5.35]

  • A process can move between queues；aging can be implemented this way → flexibility.
  • MLFQ 由以下 parameters 定義：
    1. number of queues
    2. scheduling algorithm for each queue
    3. method to upgrade a process（to higher queue）
    4. method to demote a process（to lower queue）
    5. method to determine which queue a process enters when it needs service

8.1 Slide example 規則（考試照用）[5.31] ⭐

  • Q0 – RR（slide 5.31: q = 8；例子 5.32–5.34 用 q = 4）；Q1 – RR（q = 16 / 8）；Q2 – FCFS
  • A new job always enters Q0 (RR, FCFS order)；it also preempts jobs from Q1 or Q2 currently running.
  • Gets q0​ in Q0；if not finished → moved to Q1. In Q1 gets q1​ additional；if still not complete → preempted and moved to Q2.
  • ⭐ If a job from Q1 or Q2 is preempted by a new job from Q0, it joins the HEAD of Q1 or Q2, with the remaining quantum (Q1) or remaining CPU burst (Q2).（唔會攞一個全新 quantum；唔會因為被 preempt 而 demote）
  • Q1 job 只會喺 Q0 空先跑；Q2 job 只會喺 Q0 和 Q1 都空先跑。
  • Q1 job 永遠唔會 preempt Q2 job（因為冇 process 直接 arrive 去 Q1）— summary 重點。
  • A job in Q0 is never preempted（Q0 內部只有 RR）。
  • Burst ≤q0​+q1​（e.g. 4 + 8 = 12）嘅 job 永遠唔會落 Q2。
  • This approximates SRTF：CPU-bound jobs drop like a rock；short-running I/O-bound jobs stay near the top.

8.2 Lecture example [5.32–5.34]（Q0 q=4, Q1 q=8, Q2 FCFS）

Process Arrival Burst
P1 0 10
P2 2 15
P3 5 2
P4 12 14
P5 18 6 
0 P1 4 P2 8 P3 10 P1 12 P4 16 P1 18 P5 22 P1 24 P2 32 P4 40 P5 42 P2 45 P4 47
 Q0   Q0   Q0   Q1   Q0   Q1   Q0   Q1   Q1   Q1   Q1   Q2   Q2
  • t=4 P1 用完 Q0 quantum → Q1；t=8 P2 → Q1；t=10 P3 完；P1 喺 Q1 跑；t=12 P4 到 → preempt P1（P1 返 Q1 head，剩 6 quantum）；t=16 P4 → Q1 tail；P1 繼續（剩 quantum 6）；t=18 P5 到 → preempt P1；t=22 P5 → Q1；P1 跑到 24 完成（Q1 總共用 2+2+2 = 6 ≤ 8）；P2 24–32 用完 Q1 quantum → Q2；P4 32–40 → Q2；P5 40–42 完成；P2 42–45 完；P4 45–47 完。
  • WT：P1 = 14, P2 = 28, P3 = 3, P4 = 21, P5 = 18 → avg =584​=16.8 ✔

8.3 MLFQ advantages ⭐⭐（F19 Q3.3、F20 Q2.5 必背）[5.35]

  • Used in BSD Unix, Solaris, Windows NT and later。
  1. It does not need prior knowledge of the next CPU burst time（SJF/SRTF 需要）
  2. It handles interactive jobs well — better response time than RR（short jobs 喺 top queue 完成）
  3. It produces similar performance to SJF/SRTF
  4. It is "fair" — makes progress on CPU-bound jobs
  • Starvation 可以用 reshuffling jobs periodically（e.g. 一段時間後將所有 jobs 搬返 top queue）解決。

📝 F20 Q2.5 Model answer：(1) MLFQ resembles the performance of SJF/SRTF without requiring prior knowledge of the next CPU burst time; (2) like RR, it gives good response time to interactive (short, I/O-bound) jobs since they finish in the top queues; (3) it is fair — all processes, long or short, make progress (and starvation can be avoided by periodically moving jobs up / aging). 📝 F19 Q3.3：MLFQ approximates SJF because short (interactive, I/O-bound) jobs finish within the top high-priority queue(s), while long CPU-bound jobs are demoted to lower queues — so short jobs get served first like SJF. Its major advantage over SJF is that it does not require knowing the CPU burst times in advance. ⚠️ S26 MC20 ✔「Each queue can use a different scheduling algorithm」；✗ processes never move；✗ requires burst times known；✗ non-preemptive。Sp21 MC ✔「handles interactive jobs well by delivering similar performance as SJF」；✗ needs prior knowledge；✗ classification permanent；✗ won't suffer starvation。

8.4 MLFQ 做題 checklist ✍️

  1. 每個時間點寫低：Q0、Q1、Q2 內容（同次序）、running process、佢喺邊個 queue、剩餘 quantum、剩餘 burst。
  2. 事件：arrival（入 Q0 tail；如果 running 係 Q1/Q2 → preempt，被 preempt 嘅返 head of own queue，保留剩餘 quantum）；quantum 用完（未完成 → 降一級，入 tail）；完成。
  3. Gantt 上標 process@Queue（HW2 要求 label queue）。
  4. 同一 process 由 Q0 用完 quantum 立即喺 Q1 繼續跑（因為 Q0 空）→ Gantt 可合併，但計 response time 要用 Q0 quantum 完結時間（S26 P5：49 − 45 = 4）。
  5. 題目規則永遠優先（S26 第 8 條、F20 aging timer、HW2 「retains unused quantum」）。

9. Thread Scheduling ⭐⭐ [5.36–5.37]

  • On modern OSes, kernel-level threads are scheduled (by the OS); user-level threads are managed by the thread library.
  • LWP (lightweight process) — intermediate data structure；appears as a virtual processor on which user threads are scheduled to run；each LWP attached to a kernel thread。
  • ⭐ Process-Contention Scope (PCS) — under many-to-one and many-to-many models, the thread library schedules user-level threads onto an LWP；competition among threads belonging to the same process；typically by priority set by programmers（thread library 通常唔會調整 priority）；PCS typically preempts the running thread in favour of a higher-priority user thread。
  • ⭐ System-Contention Scope (SCS) — the kernel schedules kernel threads onto an available CPU；competition among all threads in the system → 就係 CPU scheduling。
  • One-to-one systems (Windows, Linux, Solaris) schedule threads using only SCS.

📝 HW2 MC8：thread library 揀 user thread run on LWP → PCS, because the competing threads belong to the same process。 📝 F19 Q3.1：The OS schedules kernel-level threads. Mapping user threads onto kernel threads/LWPs (PCS) is done by the thread library, based on priorities set by the programmer, among the user threads of the same process; CPU scheduling (SCS) decides which kernel thread runs on a CPU among all kernel threads in the system.

10. Multiple-Processor Scheduling ⭐⭐ [5.38–5.46]

10.1 AMP vs SMP [5.38–5.39]

  • Multiprocessor 而家包括 multicore CPUs, multithreaded cores, NUMA systems, heterogeneous multiprocessing。
  • Asymmetric multiprocessing (AMP) — only one processor (the master server) accesses kernel data structures（唔使 data sharing）；all scheduling decisions, I/O processing, system activities handled by the master；other processors execute only user code；⭐ the master server can become a potential bottleneck。
  • Symmetric multiprocessing (SMP) — each processor is self-scheduling，with one common ready queue or a private ready queue per processor；每個 processor 嘅 scheduler examine ready queue 揀 thread。
    • Common queue：must ensure two processors don't choose the same thread（race condition） 同 processes 唔會 lost。
    • All modern OSes support SMP（Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, iOS）。

📝 F20 Q2.4 Model answer（common vs per-processor ready queue）：A single common ready queue achieves load balancing easily — no processor is idle while the queue is non-empty — but it is hard to keep processor affinity (a thread may run on a different CPU each time, losing its cache contents) and the shared queue needs locking (possible race condition/contention). Per-processor private ready queues naturally provide processor affinity (and no contention on a shared queue), but need extra mechanisms such as push/pull migration to balance the load.

10.2 Multicore & Multithreaded cores (CMT) ⭐ [5.40–5.44]

  • Multiple cores on the same chip — faster and consume less power, but complicate scheduling.
  • ⭐ Memory stall：when a processor accesses memory, it spends a significant amount of time waiting for data to become available（modern processors much faster than memory, esp. on cache miss）。（處理器可能 50% 時間喺等 memory）
  • Chip multithreading (CMT)（Intel = hyperthreading）：multiple hardware threads per core；each hardware thread has its own architectural state (PC, register set) and appears as a logical CPU。
  • If one thread stalls waiting for memory, the core switches to another hardware thread.
  • Dual-threaded dual-core → 4 logical processors；quad-core × 2 threads → 8 logical processors；UltraSPARC T3：16 cores × 8 threads = 128 logical processors。
  • Two levels of scheduling：
    1. OS decides which software (kernel) thread runs on each logical CPU（= CPU scheduling）
    2. Each core decides which hardware thread runs on the physical core（e.g. RR on UltraSPARC T3）
  • 三層 mapping [5.44]：user thread → LWP/kernel thread（PCS, thread library）；kernel (software) thread → logical CPU / hardware thread（CPU scheduling, OS）；hardware thread → core（core 自己，typically RR）。

📝 F19 Q2.5：multicore 優點 = faster + less power；CMT 原因 = memory stall — 一個 hardware thread 等 memory 時 core 可以跑另一個 thread（S26 MC22 ✔「another thread may run when one thread stalls waiting for memory」）。

10.3 Processor Affinity ⭐⭐ [5.45]

  • When a thread has run on a processor, that processor's cache holds its memory accesses → the thread has affinity for that processor.
  • High cost of invalidating and repopulating caches → most SMP systems try to avoid migrating processes between processors.
  • ⭐ Per-processor ready queues provide processor affinity for free!
  • Soft affinity — OS attempts to keep a process on the same processor but doesn't guarantee it（可以 migrate during load balancing）。
  • Hard affinity — a process specifies a subset of processors it may run on.（Linux：soft affinity + sched_setaffinity() for hard affinity）
  • NUMA：CPU 存取近佢嘅 memory 較快 → affinity to both processor and memory。

📝 HW2 Q2.4：hard affinity {CPU0, CPU1}，CPU2 idle → No，hard affinity must be respected；load balancing 只可以將 T 由 CPU0 搬去 CPU1。

10.4 Load Balancing ⭐ [5.46]

  • Keep workload evenly distributed（只喺 per-processor private queues 時需要）。
  • Push migration — a specific task periodically checks loads and pushes tasks from overloaded to idle/less-busy CPUs.
  • Pull migration — an idle processor pulls a waiting task from a busy processor.
  • Not mutually exclusive — often both implemented (Linux CFS).
  • ⭐ Load balancing often counteracts the benefits of processor affinity（natural tension）。
  • S26 MC22 ✗「The motivation of placing multiple cores on the same chip is to simplify the scheduler」（其實 complicate scheduling）；✔ AMP master bottleneck；✔ memory stall → run another thread；✔ affinity keeps process on same CPU for cache。

11. Real-Time CPU Scheduling ⭐⭐⭐ [5.47–5.52]

11.1 Hard vs Soft ⭐

  • Real-time scheduling demands performance guarantee — predictability.
  • Hard real-time — a task must be serviced by its deadline; service after the deadline is the same as no service.
  • Soft real-time — no guarantee when a critical real-time process will be scheduled; only guarantees it will be given preference over noncritical processes.
  • Real-time OS scheduler must support a priority-based algorithm with preemption（但 preemptive priority-based 只保證 soft real-time）。
  • Sp21 MC ✔「Soft real-time systems guarantee only that the process will be prioritized over non-critical processes」；✗ doesn't demand guarantee；✗ hard RT can service after deadline；✗ priority without preemption。

11.2 Periodic tasks [5.48]

  • 參數：processing time t, deadline d, period p，0≤t≤d≤p；rate = 1/p。
  • Admission control：process announces deadline；scheduler admits only if it can guarantee completion by the deadline。
  • CPU utilization of task i = ti​/pi​；total（U>1 → 一定有 miss）：
U=i∑​pi​ti​​

11.3 Rate-Monotonic (RM) ⭐⭐ [5.49–5.50]

  • Static priority = inverse of period：shorter period → higher priority（rationale：tasks requiring CPU more often get higher priority）。Preemptive.
  • RM is optimal among static-priority algorithms：if a set can't be scheduled by RM, no other static-priority algorithm can.
  • Only handles periodic processes with constant processing time.
  • 例 [5.49]：P1 (p=50, t=20), P2 (p=100, t=35)：U = 0.40 + 0.35 = 75% → OK：0 P1 20 P2 50 P1 70 P2 75 idle 100
  • 例 [5.50]：P1 (50, 25), P2 (80, 35)：U = 0.50 + 0.44 = 94% → 0 P1 25 P2 50 P1 75 P2 85 → P2 misses its deadline (80) by finishing at 85。
  • 課本 bound（slides 冇，但好用）：RM guaranteed if U≤N(21/N−1)：N=1 → 1；N=2 → 0.828；N=3 → 0.780；N=4 → 0.757；N→∞⇒ln2≈0.693。超過 bound 唔一定 miss（要畫 Gantt 確認）。

11.4 EDF — Earliest Deadline First ⭐⭐ [5.51–5.52]

  • Dynamic priorities according to deadline：earlier (absolute) deadline → higher priority. Preemptive。
  • 例 [5.51]（P1 50/25, P2 80/35）：0 P1 25 P2 60 P1 85 P2 100 P1 125 P2 145 idle 150 → no deadline missed（t=50 時 P2 deadline 80 < P1 新 deadline 100 → P2 繼續）。
  • EDF does not require processes to be periodic, nor a constant CPU time per burst；only requirement：announce its deadline when it becomes runnable.
  • ⭐ EDF is theoretically optimal — can meet all deadlines with CPU utilization up to 100%（但實際上 context switching + interrupt handling 令佢做唔到 100%）。
  • S26 MC21：assigns priorities according to deadlines → EDF。

📝 Sp21 Q2.3(b)：EDF is better — unlike RM with static priorities, EDF uses dynamic priorities based on deadlines, which can increase the fraction of met deadlines (schedulable up to 100% utilization). 📝 HW2 Q2.5（A: p=50,t=25；B: p=80,t=35；t=50 時 A 新 instance deadline 100，B 剩 10 deadline 80）→ No：RM 揀 A（shorter period，static）→ B 75–85 miss 80；EDF 揀 B（deadline 80 < 100）→ B 50–60 ✓，A 60–85 ✓。

11.5 RM / EDF 做題方法 ✍️

  1. 列出每個 task 嘅 release times（0, p, 2p, …）同 absolute deadlines（release + d；冇講 d 就 d = p）。
  2. 每個 time unit（或者每個事件：release / completion）揀：
    • RM：ready jobs 入面 period 最短（固定）嗰個。
    • EDF：ready jobs 入面 absolute deadline 最早嗰個。
  3. Ties：題目有講就跟（S26：smaller process ID）；冇講：keep the running job（唔 preempt）（F19、Sp21 官方答案都係咁），再唔得就 smaller ID。寫低 assumption。
  4. Soft real-time：miss 咗 deadline 嘅 job 會繼續跑完（Sp21 hint；S26 官方亦係咁），但 count 為 missed。
  5. 數 missed deadlines：每個 deadline ≤ 時限範圍嘅 job，完成時間 > deadline（或者未完成）→ miss。
  6. 先計 U=∑i​ti​/pi​ 做 sanity check。

S26 Q4.2（P1 t=1 d=3 p=4；P2 2/4/5；P3 2/6/7；P4 1/5/8；0–16，ties → smaller ID）：

  • RM（priority P1 > P2 > P3 > P4）：0 P1 1 P2 3 P3 4 P1 5 P2 7 P3 8 P1 9 P3 10 P2 12 P1 13 P3 14 P3 15 P2 16
    • P3 job (d=6) finishes 8 ✗；P4 never runs → misses d=5 ✗ and d=13 ✗；P3 job2 (d=13) finishes 14 ✗ → RM misses 4 deadlines（U = 0.25+0.4+0.286+0.125 = 1.06 > 1）
  • EDF：0 P1 1 P2 3 P4 4 P3 6 P1 7 P2 9 P1 10 P3 12 P4 13 P2 15 P1 16
    • P2 job3 (d=14) finishes 15 ✗；P1 job4 (d=15) finishes 16 ✗ → EDF misses 2 deadlines

  • RM：0 P1 1 P2 3 P1 4 P2 6 P1 7 idle 8 P2 9 P1 10 P2 11 idle 12 P1 13 P2 14
  • 兩者都冇 miss（U = 0.833）。

12. Algorithm Evaluation [5.53–5.60]

  • 先定 criteria（e.g. maximize CPU utilization subject to max response time 300 ms；maximize throughput such that TAT ∝ execution time）。
  • Deterministic modeling — takes a particular predetermined workload and defines the performance of each algorithm for that workload；simple and fast, gives exact numbers, but requires exact input and answers apply only to those cases。
    • 例 [5.54–5.55]：5 processes at t=0：P1 10, P2 29, P3 3, P4 7, P5 12 → FCFS avg WT = 28；non-preemptive SJF = 13；RR (q=10) = 23。
  • Queueing models / analysis — CPU = server with ready queue；用 distributions（exponential, described by mean）；可計 utilization、average queue length、wait time；classes of algorithms and distributions handled are limited；assumptions often unrealistic。
    • ⭐ Little's Formula：n=λ×W（n = average queue length, λ = average arrival rate, W = average waiting time in queue）；valid for any scheduling algorithm and arrival distribution（steady state，arrival rate < service rate）。
    • 例：λ=7/s, n=14⇒W=n/λ= 2 s；HW2 MC10：λ=3/s, n=12⇒W=12/3= 4 s。
  • Simulations — programming a model of the system；more accurate；data from random number generators (distributions) 或 trace files（real system 記錄）。
  • Implementation — 真系統測試，最準但 high cost & high risk；環境會變；可調 parameters；APIs 改 priority（Java, POSIX, Windows）。

13. Gantt Chart 萬用流程（考試步驟）✍️⭐⭐⭐

  1. 抄表：Process / Arrival / Burst（/ Priority）。
  2. 由 t = 0 開始逐個事件推進（events：arrival、completion、quantum expiry、check point）。每個事件寫低 ready queue（同 MLFQ 各層）。
  3. 揀 process 規則：
Algorithm 揀邊個 Preempt?
FCFS earliest arrival No
SJF shortest burst among arrived No
SRTF shortest remaining Yes, on arrival
RR head of queue Yes, quantum expiry
Priority (NP / P) highest priority P: on higher arrival
Priority + RR highest priority；same → RR Yes
MLFQ highest non-empty queue Yes（Q0 arrival preempts Q1/Q2）
RM shortest period Yes
EDF earliest absolute deadline Yes
  1. CPU idle：冇 process ready 就畫 idle（Sp21 FCFS 0 P1 2 idle 4 P2…）。
  2. 畫 Gantt：每段標 start time / process / end time；所有 boundary 時間都要寫（partial credit 靠呢個）。
  3. 計 table：Completion → TAT = C − A → WT = TAT − Burst → RT = end of first run − A。
  4. Average：寫出 na+b+⋯​=x（S26：6140​=23.33）。
  5. Sanity check：總 burst 加 idle = 最後完成時間；每個 WT ≥ 0。

13.1 Tie-breaking（寫 assumption！）

  • 同時到達、同 burst/priority：FCFS → lower process ID。
  • SRTF：新到達 burst = running remaining → 一般 keep running（唔 preempt）；F19 官方 preempt 咗，但兩種 avg WT 一樣 2.5。
  • RR：新到達 + quantum expiry 同一時刻 → 新到達先入 queue。
  • EDF：deadline 相同 → keep running，否則 smaller ID（或者跟題目）。
  • Dynamic priority（S26 Q4.3）：題目講「same priority → larger ID first」— 跟題目！

6Ch6 Synchronization同步工具

📌 考試範圍提示：Midterm 包到 Ch6（Synchronization Tools）。每年都有 1 大題（8–25 分）+ 3–4 題 MC。題型：

  1. Race condition — 列出 shared variable 所有可能值（F19 Q4.3、F20 Q5：每個值 2.5 分！）
  2. Semaphore 次序控制填空（S26 Q5：wait/signal 填 blank）、semaphore 輸出序列判斷（F19 Q4.4）
  3. 用 atomic instruction 寫 spinlock（S26 Q2.4 swap；Sp21 Q3.1 compare_and_reset）
  4. Bounded-waiting test_and_set 算法分析 / 改錯（S26 MC25、Sp21 Q3.2）
  5. 定義：race condition、critical section 三個條件、spinlock 優缺點、binary semaphore vs mutex
  6. Pthread mutex + semaphore 程式輸出（S26 MC23）

1. Background（背景）[6.4–6.8]

  • Processes execute concurrently and may be interrupted at any time, partially completing execution.
  • Concurrent access to shared data may result in data inconsistency.
  • Maintaining data consistency requires mechanisms to ensure the orderly execution of cooperating processes.

1.1 Producer–Consumer with counter [6.5–6.6]

  • 用 counter 記 buffer 有幾多 item（可以用晒 BUFFER_SIZE 格）：
/* Producer */                          /* Consumer */
while (true) {                          while (true) {
  while (counter == BUFFER_SIZE) ;        while (counter == 0) ;
  buffer[in] = next_produced;             next_consumed = buffer[out];
  in = (in + 1) % BUFFER_SIZE;            out = (out + 1) % BUFFER_SIZE;
  counter++;                              counter--;
}                                       }
  • 問題：counter++ / counter-- 唔係 atomic。

1.2 Race Condition 例子 ⭐⭐ [6.7]

counter++  →  register1 = counter;  register1 = register1 + 1;  counter = register1
counter--  →  register2 = counter;  register2 = register2 - 1;  counter = register2

counter = 5 initially，interleaving：

Step Executed Result
S0 producer: register1 = counter register1 = 5
S1 producer: register1 = register1 + 1 register1 = 6
S2 consumer: register2 = counter register2 = 5
S3 consumer: register2 = register2 − 1 register2 = 4
S4 producer: counter = register1 counter = 6
S5 consumer: counter = register2 counter = 4（正確應該係 5！）
  • 調轉 S4、S5 → counter = 6。結果取決於執行次序 → race condition。
  • Kernel race example [6.8]：P0、P1 同時 fork() → race on kernel variable next_available_pid → same pid could be assigned to two different processes unless mutual exclusion。

2. Race Condition & Critical-Section Problem ⭐⭐⭐ [6.9–6.12]

2.1 Race condition 定義（S26 Q2.1 原題，4 分）

  • Sp21 MC：「several processes access and manipulate the same data concurrently and the outcome depends on the order」→ race condition。
  • 根本原因（summary）：high-level statements (count++) translate into multiple machine instructions, which can be interleaved arbitrarily.

📝 Model answer：A race condition is an undesirable situation where several processes (or threads) access and manipulate shared data concurrently, and the final outcome depends on the particular order (timing) in which the accesses take place. Because the execution order is unpredictable (e.g., context switches at untimely points), the result can be incorrect / non-deterministic. Example: two threads execute counter++ on the same shared counter without synchronization; each loads the old value into a register, increments it and stores it back, so one update can be lost and the final value is wrong (e.g., 5 + 1 − 1 gives 4 or 6 instead of 5).

2.2 Critical Section

  • Critical section：a segment of code in which a process may be changing shared variables, updating a table, writing a file, etc.
  • When one process is in its critical section, no other may be in its critical section.（mutual exclusion and critical section imply the same thing）
  • Critical-section problem：design a protocol that processes can use to cooperate.
  • General structure [6.10]：
do {
    entry section        /* request permission */
        critical section
    exit section
        remainder section
} while (true);

2.3 三個 requirements ⭐⭐⭐（F19 Q4.1 原題）[6.11]

  1. Mutual exclusion — if process Pi​ is executing in its critical section, no other processes can be executing in their critical sections.
  2. Progress — if no process is executing in its critical section and some processes wish to enter, the selection of the process that will enter next cannot be postponed indefinitely（只有唔喺 remainder section 嘅 process 先參與決定）。
  3. Bounded waiting — a bound must exist on the number of times other processes are allowed to enter their critical sections after a process has made a request to enter its critical section and before that request is granted.（i.e. 等待時間有上限，no starvation）
  • Assumptions：each process executes at a nonzero speed；no assumption about the relative speed of the processes.
  • Summary：bounded waiting also implies progress.
  • Sp21 MC：CS solution 唔需要滿足 → synchronization（三個係 mutual exclusion, progress, bounded waiting）；mutual exclusion 定義 → A。

2.4 Critical sections in the kernel [6.12]

  • Kernel data structures（list of open files, memory allocation, process table, interrupt handling）都有 race condition。
  • Preemptive kernel — allows preemption of a process running in kernel mode；not free from race conditions，SMP 上更難；但 more responsive（適合 real-time）。
  • Non-preemptive kernel — runs until it exits kernel mode, blocks, or voluntarily yields → essentially free of race conditions in kernel mode（single-processor）。

3. Synchronization Hardware ⭐⭐ [6.13–6.21]

3.1 Disabling interrupts [6.13]

  • Uniprocessor：could simply disable interrupts → current code runs without preemption。
  • Generally inefficient on multiprocessor/SMP systems（要 disable 所有 CPU 嘅 interrupts，費時；影響 system clock）。
  • 層次：Hardware（load/store, disable interrupts, test&set, compare&swap）→ High-level APIs（locks, semaphores）→ programs。

3.2 Atomic instructions [6.14]

  • Atomic = non-interruptible；保證 instruction 唔會被中途打斷 → no race condition。
  • 即使兩個 CPU 同時執行，they are forced to execute sequentially (serialization)。
  • Building blocks for more sophisticated synchronization tools.
  • 兩個常用：test_and_set()（test a memory word and set a value）、compare_and_swap()（swap contents of two words）。
  • S26 MC24：commonly used hardware primitive → test_and_set()。

3.3 test_and_set ⭐⭐ [6.15–6.16]

boolean test_and_set(boolean *target) {   /* executed atomically */
    boolean rv = *target;
    *target = TRUE;
    return rv;                              /* returns the OLD value */
}
/* lock initialized to FALSE */
do {
    while (test_and_set(&lock)) ;   /* spin while old value was TRUE (lock held) */
        /* critical section */
    lock = false;                   /* release */
        /* remainder section */
} while (true);
  • 第一個 call 嘅 process 攞到 old = FALSE → 入 CS，同時 lock 變 TRUE；其他人攞到 TRUE → spin。
  • ✔ mutual exclusion；✘ bounded waiting（冇保證輪到邊個）。
  • Sp21 MC4（lock init 0）：entry section → while (test_and_set(&lock));（C）。✗ while (!test_and_set(&lock))。

3.4 compare_and_swap (CAS) ⭐⭐ [6.17–6.18]

int compare_and_swap(int *value, int expected, int new_value) {  /* atomic */
    int temp = *value;
    if (*value == expected)
        *value = new_value;
    return temp;                           /* returns the OLD value */
}
/* lock initialized to 0 */
do {
    while (compare_and_swap(&lock, 0, 1) != 0) ;   /* spin until old value was 0 */
        /* critical section */
    lock = 0;
        /* remainder section */
} while (true);
  • ⚠️ 留意 return 值：CAS 返回 old value → 用 != 0 判斷。Sp21 MC4 ✗ while (compare_and_swap(&lock, 0, 1) == 0)（相反）、✗ compare_and_swap(&lock, 1, 0) != 0。

3.5 Bounded-waiting Mutual Exclusion with test_and_set ⭐⭐⭐ [6.19–6.20]

/* shared: boolean waiting[n] (all false), boolean lock = false */
do {
    waiting[i] = true;
    key = true;
    while (waiting[i] && key)
        key = test_and_set(&lock);
    waiting[i] = false;
        /* critical section */
    j = (i + 1) % n;
    while ((j != i) && !waiting[j])        /* scan in cyclic order */
        j = (j + 1) % n;
    if (j == i)
        lock = false;          /* no one is waiting, so release the lock */
    else
        waiting[j] = false;    /* unblock process j (hand the lock over directly) */
        /* remainder section */
} while (true);

Sketch proof [6.20]：

  • Mutual exclusion：Pi​ enters CS only if waiting[i] == false or key == false. key becomes false only via test_and_set() — only the first process to execute test_and_set finds key == false；others wait. waiting[i] becomes false only when another process leaves its CS, and only one waiting[i] is set to false → mutual exclusion。
  • Progress：a process exiting its CS either sets lock = false or sets waiting[j] = false — both let a waiting process proceed。
  • Bounded waiting：the exiting process scans waiting[] in cyclic order (i+1, i+2, …, n−1, 0, …, i−1) and designates the first waiting one → any waiting process enters within n − 1 turns。

⚠️ S26 MC25（which is NOT correct）→ A.「test_and_set(&lock) releases the lock after the critical section」（錯：釋放係 lock = false 或者 waiting[j] = false；test_and_set 只會 set lock 為 true）。✔ waiting[i] 表示 Pi​ 想入 CS；✔ waiting[j] = false 表示 Pi​ 將 lock 交畀 Pj​（lock 冇真正釋放）；✔ 執行 lock = false 後 Pi​ 可以再入 CS。

📝 Sp21 Q3.2（改錯題）：版本用 j = i + 1; while (j < n && !waiting[j]) j++; if (j < n) waiting[j] = false; Problems：(1) 只 scan index 大過 i 嘅 process → index 細過 i 嘅 process 可能 unbounded waiting（violates bounded waiting）；(2) 冇 process 等嘅時候 lock 永遠唔會 release → 其他人之後永遠入唔到（violates progress / deadlock）。 Correction：改返 cyclic scan j = (i + 1) % n; while ((j != i) && !waiting[j]) j = (j + 1) % n; 同 if (j == i) lock = false; else waiting[j] = false;。

3.6 Atomic Variables [6.21]

  • Atomic variable：atomic (uninterruptible) updates on basic data types (integers, booleans)，用 CAS 實現：
void increment(atomic_int *v) {
    int temp;
    do {
        temp = *v;
    } while (temp != compare_and_swap(v, temp, temp + 1));   /* retry if someone changed v */
}

3.7 用其他 atomic instruction 寫 spinlock（考試題型）⭐⭐

S26 Q2.4 — swap(x, v)：atomically sets x = v and returns the old value of x（locked = 1 held / 0 free）：

while (swap(locked, 1) == 1) ;   /* acquire: spin while the old value was 1 */
/* critical section */
locked = 0;                       /* release (or swap(locked, 0)) */

Sp21 Q3.1 — compare_and_reset(int *a, int old, int new)：if (*a == old) { *a = new; return 1; } else return 0;

struct spinlock { int value = 0; };
void acquire(struct spinlock *lock) {
    while (compare_and_reset(&lock->value, 0, 1) == 0) ;   /* spin until we changed 0 → 1 */
}
void release(struct spinlock *lock) {
    lock->value = 0;
}

萬用套路：搵出「成功攞到 lock」時 instruction 嘅 return 值 → while (instruction(...) 表示失敗) ; → release 就 set 返 free value。

Instruction Acquire Release
test_and_set(&lock)（return old） while (test_and_set(&lock)) ; lock = false;
compare_and_swap(&lock, 0, 1)（return old） while (compare_and_swap(&lock, 0, 1) != 0) ; lock = 0;
swap(locked, 1)（return old） while (swap(locked, 1) == 1) ; locked = 0;
compare_and_reset(&v, 0, 1)（return 1 = success） while (compare_and_reset(&v, 0, 1) == 0) ; v = 0;
課本 swap(&lock, &key)（exchange） key = true; while (key == true) swap(&lock, &key); lock = false;

4. Mutex Locks ⭐⭐ [6.22–6.23]

  • Simplest software tool most OSes use.
  • Protect a critical region by first acquire() a lock, then release() it — both must be atomic（usually via hardware atomic instructions）。
  • Boolean variable available 表示 lock 有冇得用：
acquire() {
    while (!available) ;   /* busy wait */
    available = false;
}
release() {
    available = true;
}
do { acquire lock;  critical section;  release lock;  remainder section; } while (true);
  • This solution requires busy waiting → the lock is called a spinlock.
  • Wait if locked — 等耐咗應該 sleep / block 而唔係 spin。

4.1 Spinlock 優缺點 ⭐⭐⭐（S26 Q2.4b 原題）

  • 單 CPU 用 spinlock 冇乜意思（spin 緊嘅 thread 佔住 CPU，持有 lock 嘅 thread 跑唔到）。

📝 Model answer：Disadvantage: a spinlock wastes CPU cycles due to busy waiting (the waiting thread keeps looping). Advantage: no context switch is required when a process must wait on a lock, and a context switch may take considerable time. So spinlocks are useful when locks are expected to be held for short times, especially on multiprocessor systems, where one thread can spin on one processor while another thread executes its critical section on another processor.

5. Semaphores ⭐⭐⭐ [6.24–6.28]

5.1 定義 [6.24]

  • Semaphore S — a (non-negative) integer variable, a generalized lock；Dijkstra (late 1960s)；main synchronization primitive in original UNIX。
  • Accessed only through two atomic operations (apart from initialization)：wait() and signal()（originally P() = proberen, to test；V() = verhogen, to increment）。
  • Atomic → no more than one process can execute wait()/signal() on the same semaphore at the same time (serialization).
wait(S) {                  signal(S) {
    while (S <= 0) ;           S++;
    S--;                   }
}

5.2 Counting vs Binary [6.25] ⭐

  • Counting semaphore — value ranges over an unrestricted domain；control access to a resource with a finite number of instances（initialize to the number of available resources）；wait = 攞一個，signal = 還一個。
  • Binary semaphore — value only 0 or 1；can behave like a mutex lock，但亦可以用嚟做其他同步。
  • Ordering example（S1 喺 S2 之前執行）：synch = 0
P1:  S1;  signal(synch);          P2:  wait(synch);  S2;

📝 F19 Q4.2：Binary semaphore = mutex lock? → No. A binary semaphore initialized to 1 can be used as a mutex lock, but a binary semaphore can also be used for other synchronization purposes, e.g., initialized to 0 to enforce execution order / signaling between processes. (Also a mutex lock is owned — the thread that locks it must unlock it — whereas any process can signal a semaphore.)

5.3 Implementation with no busy waiting ⭐⭐ [6.26–6.27]

  • Each semaphore has a waiting queue（each entry：value + pointer to next record）。
  • block() — place the invoking process on the waiting queue（suspend）；wakeup(P) — remove a process from the waiting queue and put it in the ready queue。
typedef struct { int value; struct process *list; } semaphore;
wait(semaphore *S) {
    S->value--;
    if (S->value < 0) { add this process to S->list; block(); }
}
signal(semaphore *S) {
    S->value++;
    if (S->value <= 0) { remove a process P from S->list; wakeup(P); }
}
  • ⭐ Increment/decrement is done BEFORE checking the value（同 busy-waiting 版相反）。
  • ⭐ Semaphore value may become negative；if negative, its magnitude = number of processes waiting on it.（busy-waiting classical 版永遠唔會 negative）

5.4 Deadlock and Starvation ⭐ [6.28]

  • Deadlock — two or more processes waiting indefinitely for an event that can be caused only by one of the waiting processes.
S = Q = 1
P0: wait(S); wait(Q); ... signal(S); signal(Q);
P1: wait(Q); wait(S); ... signal(Q); signal(S);

P0 wait(S)、P1 wait(Q) 之後：P0 等 Q（要 P1 signal），P1 等 S（要 P0 signal）→ deadlock（extremely difficult to debug）。

  • Starvation (indefinite blocking) — a process may never be removed from the semaphore queue，例如用 LIFO order 或者按 priority 移除 queue 入面嘅 processes。

6. 做題方法 ✍️⭐⭐⭐

6.1 Race condition 所有可能值（F19 Q4.3、F20 Q5）

步驟：

  1. 將每個 thread 拆成 atomic reads/writes（c = b + a → read b, read a, write c；if 條件嘅 read 係另一個 read！）。
  2. 另一個 thread 嘅 writes 可以插喺任何 read 之間（次序保持）。
  3. 按 「條件 read 嗰陣見到嘅值」分 branch，再按「每個 read 見到新值定舊值」分 sub-case。
  4. 列出所有 distinct 值（唔好漏！每個值獨立計分）。

F19 Q4.3：a = 7, b = 2, c = 5；T1：if (a < 0) c = b - a; else c = b + a;；T2：b = 8; a = -6;

Case T1 見到 c
T2 全部喺 T1 之前 → a<0 branch b = 8, a = −6 8 − (−6) = 14
else branch；T2 喺 c 計之前完成 b = 8, a = −6 8 + (−6) = 2
else；T2 喺 T1 之後 b = 2, a = 7 9
else；write b 喺 read b 前，write a 喺 read a 後 b = 8, a = 7 15
else；read b 喺 write b 前，write a 喺 read a 前 b = 2, a = −6 −4

→ {14, 2, 9, 15, −4}

F20 Q5：a = 7, b = 2；T1：if (b < 0) c = b - a; else c = b + a;；T2：b = -8; a = 6;

  • b<0 branch（write b 喺條件 read 之前）：a 新 → −8 − 6 = −14；a 舊 → −8 − 7 = −15
  • else branch，第二次 read b 見到新值（−8）：a 新 → −8 + 6 = −2；a 舊 → −8 + 7 = −1
  • else branch，第二次 read b 見到舊值（2）：a 新 → 2 + 6 = 8；a 舊 → 2 + 7 = 9 → {−14, −15, −2, −1, 8, 9}

6.2 Semaphore 次序（dependency）題（S26 Q5）

規則：「X 必須喺 Y 之前完成」→ 用一個 init 0 嘅 semaphore s：X 完成後 signal(s)；Y 開始前 wait(s)。每個 dependency edge 一個 semaphore。

S26 Q5：A depends on B and C；B depends on C（即 C → B → A，且 C → A）；s0, s1, s2 全部 init 0。

workerA: /*BLANK1*/ wait(&s2);   wait(&s1);  printf("A");          // 等 B (s2) 同 C (s1)
workerB: /*BLANK2*/ wait(&s0);   printf("B");  signal(&s2);        // 等 C (s0)，完成通知 A
workerC: /*BLANK3*/ /* Nothing */ printf("C"); /*BLANK4*/ signal(&s0); signal(&s1);
  • BLANK1 = wait(&s2)，BLANK2 = wait(&s0)，BLANK3 = /* Nothing */，BLANK4 = signal(&s0) → 輸出一定係 C B A。

6.3 Semaphore 輸出序列題（F19 Q4.4）

semaphore L = 3, R = 0;
P1: while (true) { wait(L); putc('C'); signal(R); }
P2: while (true) { wait(R); putc('A'); putc('B'); signal(R); }
P3: while (true) { wait(R); putc('D'); }

方法：數 token。L = 3 → P1 最多印 3 個 C（冇人 signal L）。每個 C 產生 1 個 R token；P2 借 token 印 AB 後還返；P3 食咗 token 唔還。

  • (a) D 數目 = R token 總數 = 3
  • (b) A：最少 0（P3 搶晒 token），最多 infinite（P2 無限借還）
  • (c) CABABDCDABCABD → No：印到 C A B A B D C D 時 C 印咗 2 次、D 食咗 2 個 token → R = 0，下一個 A（P2 需要 wait(R)）冇 token，要等第 3 個 C 先得。
  • (d) CABACDBCABDD → Yes：C(R=1) A(P2 借→0) B(還→1) A(借→0) C(→1) D(食→0) B(還→1) C(→2) A(借→1) B(還→2) D(→1) D(→0) ✓
  • 技巧：逐個字元追蹤 semaphore 值同每個 process「做到邊」；任何時刻 token 唔可以 < 0。

6.4 Pthread 程式輸出題（S26 MC23）

int counter = 0; pthread_mutex_t mtx; sem_t sem;   /* sem_init(&sem, 0, 0) */
worker1: lock; counter += 2; printf("A %d;", counter); unlock; sem_post(&sem);
worker2: sem_wait(&sem); lock; counter += 3; printf("B %d;", counter); unlock;
  • sem 初始 0 → worker2 一定等 worker1 post → 輸出 A 2; B 5;（答案 A）。mutex 保證 counter 更新互斥。

7. 補充：Peterson（Lab 6）& classic problems（Ch7 預覽）

7.1 Peterson's Solution（two processes, software-only；Lab 6 有教 + 證明，見 Labs notes L6.1）

int turn; boolean flag[2];          /* Pi uses j = 1 - i */
do {
    flag[i] = true;  turn = j;
    while (flag[j] && turn == j) ;
        /* critical section */
    flag[i] = false;
        /* remainder section */
} while (true);
  • 滿足 mutual exclusion、progress、bounded waiting（兩個 process）；但 modern architectures may reorder instructions → not guaranteed to work without memory barriers。

7.2 Classic problems with semaphores（Ch7 預覽）

  • Bounded buffer：mutex = 1, full = 0, empty = n
Producer: wait(empty); wait(mutex); add item; signal(mutex); signal(full);
Consumer: wait(full);  wait(mutex); remove item; signal(mutex); signal(empty);
  • ⚠️ 調轉 wait(mutex) 同 wait(empty) 次序 → 可能 deadlock。
  • First readers–writers：rw_mutex = 1, mutex = 1, read_count = 0；第一個 reader wait(rw_mutex)，最後一個 reader signal(rw_mutex)；writers 可能 starve。
  • Condition variables (POSIX)：pthread_cond_wait(&cond, &mutex)（必須持有 mutex；wait 時釋放 mutex 並 sleep，醒後重新 acquire）；pthread_cond_signal(&cond)。

8. 常見陷阱 & MC 速查

敘述 真/假
Race condition: outcome depends on order of access ✔
counter++ is a single atomic machine instruction ✘
CS requirements: mutual exclusion, progress, bounded waiting ✔
"Synchronization" is one of the 3 CS requirements ✘
Bounded waiting implies progress ✔（summary）
Disabling interrupts works well on multiprocessors ✘（only uniprocessor）
Atomic = non-interruptible ✔
test_and_set returns the new value ✘（old value）
CAS returns old value ✔
Simple TAS lock satisfies bounded waiting ✘
Bounded-waiting TAS: waiting process enters within n−1 turns ✔
test_and_set releases the lock ✘
Spinlock wastes CPU but avoids context switch ✔
Spinlocks useful on multiprocessors for short critical sections ✔
Semaphore accessed only by wait/signal (except init) ✔
P() = wait, V() = signal ✔
Binary semaphore = mutex lock (equivalent) ✘（can be used as one, but more general）
Counting semaphore initialized to # of resources ✔
Blocking semaphore value can be negative = # waiting ✔
Non-preemptive kernel essentially free of race conditions (uniprocessor) ✔
LIFO semaphore queue may cause starvation ✔
Wrong order of wait() on two semaphores may deadlock ✔

10. 自我測驗

  1. 寫出 CS 三個 requirements 嘅定義（英文）。
  2. 用 test_and_set 寫 lock；點解唔滿足 bounded waiting？
  3. 一個 semaphore value = −3 代表咩？（3 個 processes 喺 waiting queue）
  4. x = 0；T1：x = x + 1；T2：x = x * 2（每句 read/write 分開）→ 可能值？（2: T1→T2；1: T2→T1；1: T1 read 0, T2 read 0 & write 0, T1 write 1；0: T2 read 0, T1 write 1, T2 write 0 → {0, 1, 2}）
  5. 三個 threads 要 A → B → C 次序，用最少 semaphores 寫出來。（s1 = s2 = 0；A; signal(s1) | wait(s1); B; signal(s2) | wait(s2); C）

L1. Lab 1 — Linux 環境 & Shell 指令

  • Terminal = 畫面/視窗；Shell = 解讀指令嘅程式（bash, tcsh…）→ shell fetches, interprets, executes commands（Ch2 [2.8]）。
  • 常用指令：
指令 用途 指令 用途
pwd 顯示目前目錄 cd dir / cd .. / cd ~ 轉目錄
ls -l -h / ls -a 列出檔案（詳細 / 包括隱藏） mkdir / rmdir 建立 / 刪除目錄
cp a b / mv a b / rm f 複製 / 搬或改名 / 刪除 cat / less / head / tail 睇檔案

L2. Lab 2 — C in Linux、編譯流程、Ch1–3 Review

L2.1 Compile pipeline（同 Ch2 linker/loader 掛鈎）

  • 最簡：gcc prog.c -o prog → ./prog（loader 將 executable 載入 memory）。
  • gcc -c main.c → main.o（relocatable object）；gcc -o main main.o -lm → linker 連 math library（-lm，用 <math.h> 時要加）。
  • -g：加 debugging info → gdb prog；Pthreads：gcc prog.c -lpthread（或 -pthread）。
  • Makefile：target: prerequisites + 下一行 TAB（唔可以用空格）+ command；make / make clean。

L2.2 I/O Subsystem 補充（Lab 2 review slides）

  • Buffering — store data temporarily while being transferred；Caching — faster device holding a copy of data。
    • ⭐ 分別：a buffer may hold the only existing copy of a data item, whereas a cache only holds a copy on faster storage of an item that resides elsewhere.
  • Spooling — hold output for a device that cannot accept interleaved data（e.g. printer）。
  • I/O hardware：port（connection point）、bus（PCI / PCIe、expansion bus for slow devices）、controller (host adapter)；device registers：data-in, data-out, status, control。
  • Device driver presents a uniform device-access interface to the I/O subsystem（abstraction）。
  • Interrupt 補充：maskable vs nonmaskable；interrupt vector = table of interrupt-handler addresses；multilevel interrupts（high vs low priority）；⭐ a trap (software interrupt) has a relatively LOW interrupt priority compared with device interrupts；multi-CPU systems can process interrupts concurrently。
  • DMA controller operates the memory bus directly — momentarily prevents the CPU from accessing main memory（cycle stealing）；完成後 interrupt。

L2.3 Lab 2 fork 題（已驗證 ✔）

int main() {
    pid_t pid = fork();  int cnt = 0;
    if (pid == 0) {
        cnt += 10;  pid = fork();
        if (pid != 0) { cnt += 10;  pid = fork(); }
    }
    printf("%d \n", pid);  printf("%d \n", cnt);
    return 0;
}
  • 4 個 processes 印出：P0（pid≠0, cnt 0）、C1（pid≠0, cnt 20）、C2（pid 0, cnt 10）、C3（pid 0, cnt 20）。
  • non-zero PID 印 2 次；'0' 印 3 次（P0 嘅 cnt + C2、C3 嘅 pid）；'10' 印 1 次。

填空：保證輸出 process 3 → 2 → 1（每個都印 x = 1）：

if (fork()) {            // BLANK1: fork()（> 0 亦可）
    x = x + 1;  wait(0); // BLANK2: wait(0) / wait(NULL)
    printf("...process 1 is %d\n", x);
} else if (fork()) {     // BLANK3: fork()
    x = x + 1;  wait(0); // BLANK4: wait(0)
    printf("...process 2 is %d\n", x);
} else { x = x + 1;  printf("...process 3 is %d\n", x); }

L3. Lab 3 — Linux Process & Pipe System Calls（⭐⭐⭐ PA1 + 考試 API）

L3.1 本 lab 用到嘅 system calls

  • Process：getpid, getppid, sleep, fork, wait, signal
  • File：open, read, write, close, pipe, dup, dup2
  • Execute：execl, execlp, execle, execv, execvp, execvpe
Call 重點
pid_t getpid(void) / getppid(void) 自己 / parent 嘅 PID
unsigned int sleep(unsigned int s) 停 s 秒（usleep 用 µs；nanosleep 更細）
pid_t fork(void) child 0、parent child PID、−1 error（set errno）；child 得到 parent address space（text, data, bss, heap, stack）同 open file descriptors 嘅獨立 copy
pid_t wait(int *status) 等任何一個 child；wait(0) / wait(NULL) 唔要 status；返回 child PID；課程只用 wait()（waitpid 唔使）
signal(SIGINT, handler) signal = software-generated interrupt；可以用 customized handler 取代 default；child inherits the customized handler

L3.2 Zombie / Orphan demo（lab 示範）

  • Orphan：parent 先完（冇 wait）→ shell prompt 出咗嚟之後 child 先繼續印 → child 被 init (PID 1) adopt & reap。
  • 用 wait() 正確：parent 印完 wait(0) → child 印完先返 shell。
  • Zombie：child 已完但 parent 仲 sleep(10) 未 wait() → child 喺嗰段時間係 zombie；parent wait(0) 後清走。
  • Exit status：voluntary — normal exit(0)（return from main / exit / _exit）、error exit(1)；involuntary — fatal error（divide by 0, segmentation fault, core dump）、killed by another process（kill()）。child 終止時：open files flushed & closed、resources de-allocated、parent notified via a signal、exit status via wait()。

L3.3 File operations（低階 vs stdio）

fd = open("hello.txt", O_CREAT | O_WRONLY, S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR);   /* permission 600 */
write(fd, "hello\n", 6);  close(fd);
fd = open("hello.txt", O_RDONLY);  read(fd, buffer, 6);  close(fd);
  • open/read/write/close（<fcntl.h>, <unistd.h>）= low-level system calls；fopen/fread/fwrite/fclose（<stdio.h>）= high-level C library。
  • ⭐ PA 唔准用 stdio file ops：FILE* 係 C library 嘅 struct，cannot be used in pipe operations。

L3.4 Pipes

  • Key concept：treat a pipe as 2 files；int pipe(int pfds[2]) → pfds[0] read end，pfds[1] write end。
  • Data received in the order it was sent；OS enforces mutual exclusion（only one process at a time）；processes sharing the pipe must have the same parent。
  • ⭐ read/write are blocking：冇 data 讀 → reader block；pipe 滿 → writer block（pipe size 有限：4 KB page / 64 KB）。
  • Two-way communication → create two pipes（每個方向一條）。
  • Shell pipe ps aux | grep root | sort | wc -l：前一個 command 嘅 output 做下一個嘅 input。

L3.5 exec family

  • 6 variants：execl, execlp, execle, execv, execvp, execvpe — replace the current process image；成功唔會 return；error return −1。
  • 字母意思：l = arguments as a list（數目已知）；v = arguments in a vector/array（compile time 唔知數目，PA1 用 execvp）；p = search PATH；e = pass environment。
execlp("ls", "ls", "-l", "-h", NULL);            /* same as running "ls -l -h" */
char *args[] = {"ls", "-l", "-h", NULL};  execvp("ls", args);
printf("never printed if exec succeeds\n");

L3.6 dup / dup2（redirection 核心）

  • int dup(int oldfd) — copy 到 first unused (lowest-numbered) fd；int dup2(int oldfd, int newfd) — copy 到指定 newfd（如已開先 close）；成功返回新 fd，失敗 −1。
  • Default：0 = stdin，1 = stdout，2 = stderr。
  • Lab 題：以下程式輸出係咩？
fd = open("output.txt", O_CREAT | O_WRONLY, S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR);
close(1);                 /* close stdout */
dup(fd);                  /* lowest free fd = 1 → stdout now refers to output.txt */
printf("Hello World!\n"); fflush(stdout);

→ 螢幕冇嘢顯示；"Hello World!" 寫入 output.txt。

  • ls | wc -l 實作（lab 版本：parent 做 wc）：
pipe(pfds);
if (fork() == 0) {                 /* child → ls */
    close(1); dup(pfds[1]);        /* stdout = pipe write end */
    close(pfds[0]);
    execlp("ls", "ls", NULL);
} else {                           /* parent → wc -l */
    close(0); dup(pfds[0]);        /* stdin = pipe read end */
    close(pfds[1]);                /* MUST close write end, else wc never sees EOF */
    wait(0);
    execlp("wc", "wc", "-l", NULL);
}
  • dup vs dup2：兩個都得；dup2 更 flexible、易讀；如果連續兩個 close 再兩個 duplicate，應該用 dup2 指定位置。

L3.7 Lab 3 fork 例題 + 更多歷屆 fork 題（全部驗證 ✔）

題目 Code（重點） 答案
Ex1 for (i=0;i<3;i++) fork(); 23=8
Ex2 for(i<2){ fork(); for(j<3) if(!fork()){} } 8 個連續 fork → 28=256
Ex3 for(i<10){ if(fork()){fork();fork();} else fork(); } 每輪 ×6（parent 4 + child 2）→ 610
Fall 2022 Q3 for(i<n){ if (fork() == fork()) printf(...); } processes 4n；lines 40+41+⋯+4n−1=34n−1​（n=1,2,3：1, 5, 21 行）
Fall 2024 P3.1 for(i<M){ pid = fork(); if(!pid) for(j<N) fork(); } (a) child 執行 line Y（!pid true）；(b) M=N=1 → 3；(c) (2N+1)M
Spring 2025 MC12 if (fork() || fork()) { if (fork() && !fork()) fork(); } 9 processes（新建 8 個）
  • Fall 2022 解釋：每輪每個 process 變 4 個（2 個 fork）→ 4n；每輪只有「兩個 fork 都返回 0」嗰個 grandchild 印 → 第 k 輪印 4k−1 行。
  • Fall 2024 解釋：設 f(k) = 剩 k 輪時一個 process 最終變幾多個：parent 自己繼續 → f(k−1)；child 做 N 次 fork 變 2N 個、每個都繼續 → 2Nf(k−1)；所以 f(k)=(1+2N)f(k−1)，f(M)=(2N+1)M。
  • Short-circuit 圖解（lab）：
Pattern 共幾多 processes 入 if-clause 入 else-clause
fork() && fork() 3 1（兩個都 > 0） 2
fork() || fork() 3 2 1（兩個都 = 0）
  • S25 MC12：外層 || → 2 個入 if、1 個入 else；內層 fork() && !fork() → 1 個入 inner if（再 fork → 2）、2 個唔入 → 每個變 4 → 2×4+1=9。
  • Tips（lab）：見到 loop → 展開成冇 loop 嘅等價 statements；nested loop → 先展開內層；if (fork()) → 分別諗 parent 同 child 行咩。

L3.8 PA1 — Simplified Linux Shell（考試可能問）

  • 6 種 command pattern：cmd、cmd < in、cmd > out、cmd < in > out、cmd > out < in、cmd1 | cmd2 | …（最多 8 段）。
  • cd 唔可以用 exec 做（要改 shell 自己嘅 working directory）→ chdir(path)（0 成功 / −1 失敗）。
  • 唔准用 system() / popen()（會開另一個 shell 代你做）。
  • Redirection = open + dup/dup2 取代 stdin/stdout；multi-level pipe = 將 2-level pipe 寫成 for-loop。
  • execvp 嘅 argv array 尾要放 NULL（所以 8 個 arguments 要 size 9）。
  • Ctrl-C → signal(SIGINT, handler)，SIGINT = 2；start/end PID 要一致（冇多餘 processes）。
  • Plagiarism：JPlag 檢測，提供同抄襲雙方都 0 分。

L4. Lab 4 — Named Pipes & Pthreads

L4.1 Anonymous vs Named pipes（lab 版本）

  • Anonymous：unidirectional；cannot be accessed outside the creating process；parent–child；ceases after processes terminate。
  • Named (FIFO)：bidirectional；no parent–child needed；several processes（多 writers）；appear as files（mkfifo()）；exist until explicitly deleted。
  • ⭐ FIFO 細節：
    • open / read / write 係 blocking：FIFO 要兩端都有 process open 先會 unblock（冇 reader 時 writer 會 block）；用 O_NONBLOCK 可以變 non-blocking。
    • Data read once then discarded（唔似 regular file 可以重讀）→ cannot broadcast to multiple recipients。
    • 實際上 一條 FIFO 唔適合雙向（寫完即刻讀可能讀返自己個 message）→ 雙向用兩條。
    • Writes ≤ PIPE_BUF bytes are atomic；更大可能同其他 writer 交錯。
  • popen(cmd, "r"/"w") / pclose(fp)（<stdio.h>）：fork 一個 child 執行 cmd，返回 FILE* 連住佢嘅 stdout（"r"）或 stdin（"w"）；pclose 等佢完並返回 termination status。（PA1 禁用）
  • FIFO producer：if (access(FIFO_NAME, F_OK) == -1) mkfifo(FIFO_NAME, 0777); → open(FIFO_NAME, O_WRONLY) → write loop → close；consumer：open(..., O_RDONLY) → read until 0 → close。
  • access(path, how)：F_OK 存在、R_OK/W_OK/X_OK 權限；0 = OK，−1 = 唔得。

L4.2 Exam example — 兩條 ordinary pipes 雙向通訊（填空）

char buffer[10] = {};  int p2c[2], c2p[2];
pipe(p2c);                                  /* BLANK1 */
pipe(c2p);                                  /* BLANK2 */
pid_t pid = fork();
if (pid == 0) {                             /* child */
    const char msg[] = "Child";
    close(c2p[0]);
    write(c2p[1], msg, 6);                  /* BLANK3（5 亦接受） */
    close(p2c[1]);
    read(p2c[0], buffer, 7);                /* BLANK4（6 亦接受） */
    printf("Child received the message: %s\n", buffer);
} else {                                    /* parent */
    const char msg[] = "Parent";
    close(c2p[1]);
    read(c2p[0], buffer, 6);                /* BLANK5（5 亦接受） */
    close(p2c[0]);
    write(p2c[1], msg, 7);                  /* BLANK6（6 亦接受） */
    printf("Parent received the message: %s\n", buffer);
}
  • 輸出：Parent received the message: Child / Child received the message: Parent。

L4.3 Pthreads

int sum;                                   /* shared by the threads */
void *runner(void *param) {
    int upper = atoi(param);  sum = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i <= upper; i++) sum += i;
    pthread_exit(0);
}
int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    pthread_t tid;  pthread_attr_t attr;
    pthread_attr_init(&attr);                       /* default attributes */
    pthread_create(&tid, &attr, runner, argv[1]);   /* id, attr, start routine, arg */
    pthread_join(tid, NULL);                        /* wait for the thread */
    printf("sum = %d\n", sum);
}
  • pthread_t = thread id；pthread_attr_t = attributes（stack size, scheduling info）；compile -lpthread。
  • Join 多個 threads：for (i = 0; i < 10; i++) pthread_join(workers[i], NULL);
  • Thread trace：main 印 "main: begin" → create T1、T2 → join → "main: end"；threads run independently, order depends on scheduling（T2 可以喺 T1 之前行）。
  • 兩個 threads 各印 "begin of X" 同 "end of X" → 中間 4 行有 (24​)=6 種次序（每個 thread 自己 begin 先過 end），"main: start" 最先、"main: finish" 最尾 → 6 possible outputs。

L4.4 Exam example — thread vs process 共享 memory（MC）

void *child(void *arg) { int *counter = (int *)arg; (*counter)++; return NULL; }
int main() {
    int counter = 0;  pthread_t thread;
    pthread_create(&thread, NULL, child, (void *)&counter);
    pthread_join(thread, NULL);
    printf("%d\n", counter);                 /* 1: thread shares memory */
    counter = 0;
    pid_t pid = fork();
    if (pid) wait(NULL);
    else { child((void *)&counter); exit(0); }
    printf("%d\n", counter);                 /* 0: child process has its own copy */
}
  • 選項 A 0 0、B 1 0、C 0 1、D 1 1 → 答案 B（1 / 0）。Key：threads share memory space but processes have separate memory spaces.

L5. Lab 5 — Scheduling Review & PA2（MLFQ）

L5.1 Review 例題（P1 7, P2 4, P3 1, P4 4，全部 t=0，已驗證 ✔）

Algorithm Gantt avg WT
FCFS / RR q=8 0 P1 7 P2 11 P3 12 P4 16 40+7+11+12​=7.5
RR q=4 0 P1 4 P2 8 P3 9 P4 13 P1 16 49+4+8+9​=7.5
RR q=2 0 P1 2 P2 4 P3 5 P4 7 P1 9 P2 11 P4 13 P1 16 49+7+4+9​=7.25
SJF 0 P3 1 P2 5 P4 9 P1 16（P2、P4 同長 → 先 P2） 49+1+0+5​=3.75
Priority（4,1,2,3） 0 P2 4 P3 5 P4 9 P1 16 49+0+4+5​=4.5
  • SRTF（P1 0/7, P2 2/4, P3 4/1, P4 5/4）：0 P1 2 P2 4 P3 5 P2 7 P4 11 P1 16 → 49+1+0+2​=3。
  • 觀察：q 大過最長 burst → RR = FCFS；q 細咗 avg WT 唔一定變差（7.25 < 7.5）。

L5.2 ⭐ Priority + RR 有唔同 arrival time（HW / Exam 熱門）

  • ⚠️ Common mistake：reset the time quantum of a preempted process. 正確：被高 priority 新 process preempt 嘅 process 要記住佢剩餘嘅 quantum（同 MLFQ 規則一樣）。
  • Spring 2023 midterm 官方答案（q = 2）：0 P1 1 P2 4 P1 5 P3 7 P1 8 P4 10 P1 11 P3 13 P5 15 P1 16 P3 18 P5 20 P3 22 P5 24
    • P1 喺 0–1 跑咗 1 unit 被 P2（高 priority）preempt → 4–5 只跑剩低嘅 1 unit quantum 然後輪到 P3（同 priority RR）。8–10 同樣：P4 preempt P1，P1 10–11 用返剩低 1 unit。
    • 由 Gantt 推返嘅 table（模擬器重現完全一致 ✔）：P1 (0, 5, pr 2)、P2 (1, 3, pr 1)、P3 (2, 8, pr 2)、P4 (8, 2, pr 1)、P5 (9, 6, pr 2)，細數字 = 高 priority。

L5.3 RM / EDF 例題（deadline < period）

  • P1 (t=1, d=2, p=4)、P2 (2, 5, 6)、P3 (3, 7, 9)；U=41​+62​+93​=0.917。
  • RM（P1 > P2 > P3）：0 P1 1 P2 3 P3 4 P1 5 P3 6 P2 8 P1 9 P3 … → P3 first job finishes at 10 > deadline 7 → misses 1 deadline。
  • EDF：0 P1 1 P2 3 P3 4 P1 5 P3 7 P2 8 P1 9 P2 10 P3 12 … → no deadline missed。

L5.4 PA2 — N-level MLFQ simulator

  • N = 1–4 queues，last queue must be FCFS（input 用大數 e.g. 1000 代表 FCFS），≤ 10 processes。
  • Input：queue_num = 3、time_quantum = 2 4 1000、process_table_size、process_table（P1 0 7 …）；# 開頭 / 空行忽略。
  • Assumptions：sorted by arrival；first arrival = 0；no two processes arrive at the same time；CPU never idle；Gantt ≤ 300 steps。
  • 用法：./mlfq < input.txt > output.txt（input/output redirection）；用 diff --side-by-side your-out.txt sample-out.txt（--suppress-common-lines）對答案。
  • Output：parsed values + Gantt Chart = 0 P1 2 P2 3 P1 4 P3 5 P1 6 P4 8 P1 10 P4 11 P1 12。
  • Step-by-step 例子（Q0 q=2, Q1 q=4, Q2 FCFS；P1 0/7, P2 1/1, P3 4/1, P4 6/3），已用模擬器驗證 ✔：
    • t=1 P2 到 → no preemption（P1 都喺 Q0）；t=2 P1 用完 Q0 quantum → Q1；P2 跑。
    • t=3 P2 完 → P1（Q1，quantum 4）；t=4 P3 到 → P1 preempted（剩 burst 4，剩 quantum 3）。
    • t=5 P3 完 → P1；t=6 P4 到 → P1 preempted（剩 quantum 2）；P4 6–8 用完 Q0 → Q1 tail。
    • t=8 Q1 = [P1, P4] → P1 跑 2 → quantum 用完（剩 burst 1）→ Q2；t=10 P4 跑 1 完；t=11 P1（Q2）跑到 12。

L6. Lab 6 — Synchronization Review（Sample Questions）

L6.1 Peterson's solution（software-only，2 processes）

/* P_i (j = 1 - i) */
do {
    flag[i] = true;  turn = j;
    while (flag[j] && turn == j) ;   /* busy wait */
        /* critical section */
    flag[i] = false;
        /* remainder section */
} while (true);
  • Shared：flag[2]（想入 CS）、turn（輪到邊個）；assumption：load and store are atomic。
  • Proof：ME — 兩個都想入時 turn 只可以係 0 或 1 → 只有一個過到 while；Progress — 冇人喺 CS 就即刻入；Bounded waiting — 最多等對方一次（對方出嚟會設 flag[j] = false，再想入就要設 turn = i）。
  • 缺點：複雜（只限兩個 process）、每個 thread code 唔同、busy waiting 浪費 CPU → OS 提供 mutex / semaphore / condition variable。

L6.2 POSIX primitives 速查

  • Mutex：pthread_mutex_init(&m, NULL) → lock → access → unlock → destroy；thread 持 lock 時 crash → 其他人 block。
  • Semaphore（<semaphore.h>）：sem_init(&s, pshared, value)（pshared = 0：同一 process 嘅 threads 共用）、sem_wait、sem_post、sem_destroy。
Initial value 行為 用途
1 一個 permit mutual exclusion（當 mutex）
0 wait() 一定 block 直至有人 signal ordering（等其他 thread 做完先）
N N 個 permits 管理 N 個相同 resources
  • Condition variable：pthread_cond_wait(&cond, &mutex) atomically releases the mutex and sleeps；signalled → re-acquires the mutex before returning；用 while (!ready) 包住；pthread_cond_signal / pthread_cond_broadcast。
  • Lab note：semaphore ≈ integer S + a mutex protecting it + a condition variable whose condition is "S > 0"。

L6.3 Sample Questions（官方答案，已驗證 ✔）

  • Q0：binary semaphore = mutex？→ No — init 1 可以當 mutex，但 init 0 可以做其他用途（ordering）。
  • Q1：T1：wait(S1); CS; signal(S2)；T2：wait(S2); CS; signal(S3)；T3：wait(S3); CS; signal(S1) 要 T1, T2, T3, T1… → S1 = 1, S2 = 0, S3 = 0。
  • Q2（P0 → P1 → P2 循環，填 BLANK）：S0 = 1, S1 = 0, S2 = 0；P0：wait(S0) … signal(S1)；P1：wait(S1) … signal(S2)；P2：wait(S2) … signal(S0)。
  • Q3（mutex 填空）：pthread_mutex_t* m = (pthread_mutex_t*) arg;、pthread_mutex_lock(m);、pthread_mutex_unlock(m); → purpose：protect the shared counter；final counter = 10,000（兩個 threads 各加 5,000）。（void* 要 cast 返 pthread_mutex_t*，因為 thread function signature 一定係 void *f(void *)。）
  • Q4（X = Y = 0）：A：wait(X); "b"; signal(Y); wait(Y); "c"; signal(Y); B：signal(X); "a"; wait(Y); "d";
    • Both complete：abcd, bacd, bcad（3 種）；如果 B 先攞到 Y → A 永遠 block → bad, abd（A 唔會完成）。
  • Q5（S0 = 1, S1 = S2 = S3 = 0）：P0 loop：wait(S0); print '1'; release(S1); release(S2); release(S3);；P1：wait(S1); release(S0);；P2：wait(S2); release(S0); wait(S3); release(S0); → '1' 印 4 次（S0 permits：initial 1 + P1 1 + P2 2 = 4）。
  • Q6（readers–writers，用兩個 mutex）：
/* reader */
pthread_mutex_lock(&mutex);
read_count++;
if (read_count == 1) pthread_mutex_lock(&rw_mutex);    /* first reader locks out writers */
pthread_mutex_unlock(&mutex);
    /* reading */
pthread_mutex_lock(&mutex);
read_count--;
if (read_count == 0) pthread_mutex_unlock(&rw_mutex);  /* last reader lets writers in */
pthread_mutex_unlock(&mutex);
/* writer */
pthread_mutex_lock(&rw_mutex);  /* writing */  pthread_mutex_unlock(&rw_mutex);
  • Q7（race values）：a = 1, b = 3, c = 0；T1：a = b + 1; c = a - b;；T2：a = 13; b = 10; c = 2; → c ∈ {−6, 1, 2, 3, 10}。
    • 2：T2 嘅 c = 2 最後寫；1：T1 讀 a=4、b=3 後 T2 全做完，或者 T2 先全做（a = 11, c = 11 − 10）；−6：T1 讀 a=4 後 T2 全做（b=10）；3：T1 寫 a=4 → T2 全做 → T1 讀 a=13, b=10；10：T1 寫 a=4 → T2 寫 a=13 → T1 讀 a=13, b=3 → T2 寫 b, c → T1 寫 c = 10。
    • 方法：列出每個 read 可能見到嘅值（a ∈ {4, 11, 13}, b ∈ {3, 10}）+ 邊個最後寫 c，再剔走不可能組合（a=11 表示 b 已經係 10）。

L7. 常見陷阱（Labs / PA）

敘述 真/假
PA 可以用 fopen/FILE* 做 pipe ✘（FILE* 唔用得喺 pipe operations）
wait(0) 同 wait(NULL) 一樣 ✔
dup(fd) 一定返回 1 ✘（返回 lowest unused fd；要先 close(1)）
exec*() 成功後會返回 0 ✘（唔會 return；失敗 −1）
execvp 嘅 argv 唔使 NULL 結尾 ✘
cd 可以用 execvp("cd", …) 做 ✘（要 chdir）
FIFO 開 write end 時冇 reader 會 block ✔
FIFO 啲 data 可以畀多個 reader 各讀一次（broadcast） ✘
Child 會繼承 parent 嘅 customized signal handler ✔
Threads share memory，processes 唔 share ✔
Priority + RR 被 preempt 後 quantum 重新計 ✘（保留剩餘 quantum）
PA2：最後一層 queue 係 FCFS ✔
Peterson：assume load/store atomic ✔
sem_init(&s, 0, 0) 嘅 0（第二個）表示 threads 共用 ✔（pshared = 0）
Condition wait 會放開 mutex ✔（醒返會重新攞）

QPast Papers Solved歷屆長題全解

Spring 2026 Midterm（lecturer 提供）

S26-Q2.1 Race condition (4 pts) CH6

What is a race condition? Give an example.

Answer.

A race condition occurs when two or more processes/threads access and manipulate shared data concurrently, and the final result depends on the order in which the accesses take place; since the order is unpredictable, the result may be incorrect or inconsistent. (2.5) Example: two threads increment the same counter without synchronization — counter++ is load/add/store, so both may load the same old value and one update is lost. (1.5)

S26-Q2.2 Caching (4 pts) CH1

What is the fundamental idea of caching? Is a high cache hit ratio alone enough to guarantee good performance? Explain by considering hit time and miss penalty.

Answer.

Caching temporarily copies a subset of information from a slower but larger storage into a faster but smaller storage so that frequently used data can be accessed more quickly. (2) No — hit ratio is a major criterion but not sufficient (1); performance is the average access time = hit ratio × hit time + miss ratio × miss time, which also depends on the hit time and the miss penalty (1). A slow cache or a huge miss penalty can still give poor performance.

S26-Q2.3 Custom policy fᵢ = 1/(a·cᵢ + b) (4 pts) CH5

The OS keeps ci​ = average past CPU burst of Pi​ and picks the process with the highest fi​=aci​+b1​ (a,b>0), running it for one quantum or until it gives up the CPU. (a) Does this prioritize I/O-bound over CPU-bound processes? (b) Can it cause starvation?

Answer.

(a) Yes — I/O-bound processes have small CPU bursts ci​, hence a larger fi​ and higher priority. (b) Yes — a CPU-bound process (large ci​, low fi​) can starve if higher-priority I/O-bound processes keep arriving.

S26-Q2.4 swap spinlock (4 pts) CH6

swap(x, v) atomically sets x to v and returns the old value of x. locked = 1 when held, 0 otherwise. (a) Write the line that acquires the spinlock with a busy-spin loop. (b) Advantage and disadvantage of a spinlock.

Answer.

(a) while (swap(locked, 1) == 1); (release: locked = 0;) (b) Disadvantage: wastes CPU cycles due to busy waiting. Advantage: no context switch is needed when a process must wait on a lock (a context switch can take considerable time) — good for short critical sections on multiprocessors.

S26-Q3.1 fork tree with break (8 pts) CH3
for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (fork()) fork();
    else break;
}

(a) n = 2: draw the process tree; total processes and number of breaks. (b) Relationship between total processes and n.

Answer.

(a) 7 processes, 3 breaks. Tree: P0 → P1 (break), P2, P3 (break), P4; P2 → P5 (break), P6. (b) Each active process per iteration creates 2 children: the first breaks, the second keeps looping → active count doubles: Ak​=2k. After n iterations: active =2n, stopped =1+2+⋯+2n−1=2n−1. Total =2n+1−1 (breaks =2n−1).

S26-Q3.2 fork + exec scenarios (8 pts) CH3
int ret = fork();
if (ret == 0) { printf("Hello1\n"); exec("some_executable"); printf("Hello2\n"); }
else if (ret > 0) { wait(NULL); printf("Hello3\n"); }
else { printf("Hello4\n"); }

List all possible scenarios and outputs.

Answer.
  • Case I — fork succeeds, exec succeeds: Hello1, Hello3 (exec replaces the image; Hello2 never runs).
  • Case II — fork succeeds, exec fails (returns −1): Hello1, Hello2, Hello3.
  • Case III — fork fails: Hello4. (Hello3 always last because the parent waits.)

  • Blank 5.1: fd[0] · 5.2: &child_cnt (parent: read(fd[0], &child_cnt, sizeof(int)))

Fall 2019 Midterm

F19-Q1.1 Linker and loader (2 pts) CH2

What do the linker and loader do, respectively?

Answer.

The linker combines relocatable object files (and libraries) into a single binary executable file; the loader loads the binary executable file into memory so it can run.

F19-Q1.2 Locality (3 pts) CH1

What are temporal locality and spatial locality?

Answer.

Temporal locality: a memory location accessed recently is likely to be accessed again in the near future. Spatial locality: locations near a recently accessed location are likely to be accessed soon.

F19-Q1.3 Why separate API and system calls (2 pts) CH2

Two reasons for separating APIs from the underlying system calls?

Answer.

(1) Program portability — the API stays the same across platforms. (2) Hide the complex details of system calls from programmers.

F19-Q1.4 LKM vs layered (3 pts) CH2

Similarity and difference between the loadable-kernel-module approach and the layered approach?

Answer.

Similarity: functionality is divided into modules, each with a well-defined interface. Difference: LKM is more flexible — any module can call any other module (no higher/lower layer restriction), and modules can be loaded/removed at run time.

F19-Q2.1 State transitions (3 pts) CH3

Fill in the actions for: running→ready, ready→running, running→waiting, waiting→ready.

Answer.

running→ready: interrupt; ready→running: scheduler dispatch (CPU scheduling); running→waiting: I/O or event wait; waiting→ready: I/O or event completion.

F19-Q2.2 Socket (2 pts) CH3

Four pieces of information that uniquely define a socket connection?

Answer.

Source IP address, source port number, destination IP address, destination port number.

F19-Q2.3 Thread unique vs shared (3 pts) CH4

Three elements unique to each thread and three shared.

Answer.

Unique: program counter, registers (state), stack (thread ID). Shared: code, data (globals/heap), open files.

F19-Q2.4 Shell system calls (3 pts) CH3

Two system calls a shell must execute to start a new process on UNIX?

Answer.

fork() — clones the calling process (creates a child); exec() — overlays/replaces the child's address space with a new program (loads the program to run).

F19-Q2.5 Multicore vs SMP, CMT (4 pts) CH5

Two advantages of multicore vs conventional SMP; reason for chip multithreading (hyper-threading).

Answer.

Multicore is faster (on-chip communication) and consumes less power than separate single-core chips. CMT exploits memory stall: processors are much faster than memory, so a core may spend up to ~50% of its time waiting for data; with multiple hardware threads the core switches to another thread while one waits.

for (i = 0; i < n; ++i) { if (fork()) printf("Fork!\n"); else printf("Fork!\n"); }
Answer.

Each iteration doubles the processes and every process prints one line: iteration i prints 2i lines → total 2+4+⋯+2n=2n+1−2 ✔

if (fork() == fork() || fork() != fork()) fork();
printf("Fork!\n");
Answer.

23. After fork()==fork() there are 4 processes; only the one that got 0 twice is true → it skips the rest of || and forks → 2 lines. The other 3 run fork()!=fork() → 12 processes; 9 are true and fork again → 18; 3 false → 3. Total 2 + 18 + 3 = 23 ✔

F19-Q3.1 Which threads does the OS schedule (4 pts) CH5

Which threads are scheduled by the OS? How does mapping user threads onto kernel threads/LWPs differ from CPU scheduling?

Answer.

The OS schedules kernel-level threads. Scheduling user threads onto LWPs/kernel threads (PCS) is done by the thread library, usually by programmer-set priority, among threads of the same process; CPU scheduling (SCS) chooses which kernel thread runs on a CPU among all kernel threads in the system.

F19-Q3.2 FCFS problem; RR worse than FCFS (3 pts) CH5
Answer.

FCFS: convoy effect — short processes stuck behind a long one. RR has worse turnaround than FCFS when all processes have the same CPU burst length that is larger than the quantum (they all finish near the end).

F19-Q3.3 MLFQ approximates SJF (3 pts) CH5
Answer.

Short interactive jobs finish in the top (high-priority) queue, while long CPU-bound jobs sink to lower queues — so short jobs are served first, like SJF. Advantage: no prior knowledge of CPU burst times is needed.

Different: under LUF a process that has already run a long time is likely to starve; under SRTF a process with a long burst is likely to starve from the beginning.

F19-Q4.1 CS requirements (4 pts) CH6
Answer.

(1) Mutual exclusion — if a process is executing in its CS, no other process can be in its CS. (2) Progress — if no process is in its CS and some want to enter, the selection of the next one cannot be postponed indefinitely. (3) Bounded waiting — there is a bound on the number of times other processes may enter their CS after a process has requested entry and before that request is granted.

F19-Q4.2 Binary semaphore vs mutex (3 pts) CH6
Answer.

No. A binary semaphore initialised to 1 can be used as a mutex lock, but it can also be used for other synchronization purposes (e.g., initialised to 0 for ordering/signalling).

Fall 2020 Midterm

F20-Q2.1 Microkernel (4 pts) CH2
Answer.

Main idea: remove all nonessential components from the kernel and implement them as system/user-level programs in separate address spaces; communicate by message passing. Advantage: small kernel, easier to extend and port, more secure and reliable. Disadvantage: performance suffers due to increased system-function overhead (user↔kernel message passing).

F20-Q2.2 Linker and loader (4 pts) CH2
Answer.

Linker: combines several relocatable object modules into a single binary executable image (stored on disk). Loader: loads the executable into memory for execution.

F20-Q2.3 Heavyweight vs lightweight (4 pts) CH4
Answer.

A process is heavyweight because it owns an address space and resources; creating one duplicates program and data. A thread is lightweight — only an execution unit (PC, registers, stack) that shares code, data and files with other threads of its process, so creating it needs no duplication.

F20-Q2.4 Common vs per-processor ready queue (4 pts) CH5
Answer.

Common queue: easy load balancing (no CPU idle while the queue is non-empty) but hard to keep processor affinity (and needs locking). Per-processor queues: natural processor affinity but need push/pull migration for load balancing.

F20-Q2.5 MLFQ benefits (4 pts) CH5
Answer.

(1) Resembles SJF/SRTF performance without prior knowledge of the next CPU burst (2 pts); (2) RR-like good response time for interactive jobs (1); (3) fair — all processes make progress (1).

Sp21-Q3.1 compare_and_reset spinlock (4 pts) CH6
Answer.

struct spinlock { int value = 0; }; · acquire: while (compare_and_reset(&lock->value, 0, 1) == 0) ; · release: lock->value = 0;

Sp21-Q3.2 Fix the bounded-waiting algorithm (7 pts) CH6
Answer.

Problems: (1) only processes with index > i are checked → lower-index processes can wait unboundedly; (2) the lock is never released when nobody is waiting. Fix: cyclic scan j = (i + 1) % n; while ((j != i) && !waiting[j]) j = (j + 1) % n; if (j == i) lock = 0; else waiting[j] = false;

Homework 1（Fall 2026）

HW1-Q2.1 AMAT + locality (6 pts) CH1

Hit ratio 90%, hit time 2 ns, miss time 50 ns.

Answer.

0.9×2+0.1×50= 6.8 ns. Temporal: recently accessed items are likely accessed again (e.g., loop counter, loop body instructions). Spatial: items near recent accesses are likely accessed soon (e.g., sequential array elements a[i], a[i+1]).

HW1-Q2.2 Multiprogramming vs time sharing (6 pts) CH1
Answer.

Multiprogramming keeps several jobs in memory; when one waits for I/O, the CPU switches to another, so the CPU always has work → higher utilization. Time sharing switches among jobs so frequently (timer + CPU scheduling) that users can interact with each program while it runs → short response time, interactive computing.

HW1-Q2.3 State sequence (6 pts) CH3
Answer.

New → Ready → Running → Waiting → Ready → Running → Ready → Running → Terminated. When leaving Running, the PCB saves the process state, program counter, CPU registers, plus updated scheduling, accounting and I/O-status information.

HW1-Q2.4 read(): user → kernel → user (6 pts) CH2
Answer.

(1) read() in libc puts the system-call number and parameters in registers and executes a trap instruction. (2) The trap switches to kernel mode; the kernel indexes the system-call table and runs the read service. (3) The kernel stores the return value and executes return-from-trap, which switches back to user mode and resumes after the call.

HW1-Q2.5 Parent → child through a pipe (6 pts) CH3
Answer.

Call pipe(fd) before fork(); after fork, the parent (writer) closes fd[0] and writes to fd[1]; the child (reader) closes fd[1] and reads from fd[0]; close the used ends when done.

HW1-Q3.1 Values of x (15 pts) CH3
Answer.

C1: 3, C2: 5, P: 2 (each process has its own copy of x). Outputs: "C1: 3, C2: 5, P: 2" or "C2: 5, C1: 3, P: 2". Moving the first wait before x *= 2 guarantees C1, C2, P order; values unchanged.

HW1-Q3.2 exec worker (15 pts) CH3
Answer.

3 processes (parent → child → grandchild; the grandchild execs worker). X is not printed (successful exec never returns). Outputs: A P W C D · A W P C D · A W C P D.

HW1-Q3.3 Pipe parent → child (10 pts) CH3
Answer.

(a) Parent closes fd[0], writes to fd[1]; child closes fd[1], reads fd[0]; parent → child. (b) "Child: 12" then "Parent: done" — read blocks until data arrives, and the parent waits for the child. (c) No — separate pipe() calls after fork create two unrelated pipes, with no shared descriptors.

Homework 2（Fall 2026）

HW2-Q2.1 Different PC/registers (6 pts) CH4
Answer.

Yes — each thread has its own PC, register set and stack; saved in its TCB when not running.

HW2-Q2.2 Many-to-one on 4 cores (6 pts) CH4
Answer.

No — all user threads map to one kernel thread, which runs on one core at a time; only concurrency, no parallelism (and one blocking call blocks all).

HW2-Q2.3 Ctrl+C (6 pts) CH4
