Asynchronous (generated by an event external to the process). Yes — install a user-defined handler with signal(SIGINT, handler) to override the default (terminate).

Answer.

No — hard affinity restricts T to CPU 0 and CPU 1; load balancing may move it between those two only.

Q0 RR4, Q1 RR8, Q2 FCFS; P1 (0, 20), P2 (1, 5), P3 (11, 2); preempted Q1 job keeps the unused part of its quantum.

Answer.

0 P1(Q0) 4 P2(Q0) 8 P1(Q1) 11 P3(Q0) 13 P1(Q1) 18 P2(Q1) 19 P1(Q2) 27. At t = 11, P1 goes to the head of Q1 (ahead of P2) with 5 ms of its Q1 quantum left.

Fall 2022 Midterm（lab slides 引用）

F22-Q3 fork() == fork() in a loop (10 pts) CH3
int main() {
    int i, n;
    scanf("%d", &n);
    for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (fork() == fork()) {
            printf("fork() == fork()!\n");
            fflush(stdout);
        }
    }
    return 0;
}

(a) Number of processes and of printed lines for n = 1, 2, 3. (b) In terms of n.

Answer.

(a) n = 1: 4 processes, 1 line; n = 2: 16, 5; n = 3: 64, 21. (b) Each iteration every process does two forks → ×4, so 4n processes. In each iteration only the grandchild that received 0 from both forks sees equal return values, so the iteration that starts with 4k processes prints 4k lines. Total lines =40+41+⋯+4n−1=34n−1​. ✔ (verified)

Fall 2024 Midterm（lab slides 引用）

F24-P3.1 fork in nested loops (10 pts) CH3
for (i = 0; i < M; i++) {
    pid_t pid = fork();          // line X
    if (!pid) {
        for (j = 0; j < N; j++)  // line Y
            fork();
    }
}

(a) Which process executes line Y? (b) M = N = 1: how many processes? (c) In terms of M and N.

Answer.

(a) The child — !pid is true only where fork() returned 0. (b) 3 — the parent forks a child (2), the child forks once in the inner loop (3). (c) Let f(k) be the number of processes one process becomes with k outer iterations left: the parent continues (f(k−1)) and the child becomes 2N processes that all continue (2Nf(k−1)), so f(k)=(2N+1)f(k−1) and the total is (2N+1)M. ✔ (verified)

Spring 2025 Midterm（lab slides 引用）

S25-MC12 Nested short-circuit forks CH3
if (fork() || fork()) {
    if (fork() && !fork()) {
        fork();
    }
}

How many processes are there in total (suppose all fork() succeed)?

Answer.

9. fork() || fork(): 2 processes enter the if-clause, 1 the else-clause. Inside, fork() && !fork(): 1 process enters the inner if and forks once (→ 2), 2 processes skip it → each outer-if process becomes 4. Total 2×4+1=9 (8 newly created). ✔ (verified)

Spring 2023 Midterm（lab slides 引用）

S23-PRR Preemptive priority + RR with different arrivals (q = 2) CH5

Smaller number = higher priority; processes with equal priority share the CPU round-robin with q = 2; a higher-priority arrival preempts. Process table reconstructed from the official answer: P1 (0, 5, 2), P2 (1, 3, 1), P3 (2, 8, 2), P4 (8, 2, 1), P5 (9, 6, 2).

Answer.

0 P1 1 P2 4 P1 5 P3 7 P1 8 P4 10 P1 11 P3 13 P5 15 P1 16 P3 18 P5 20 P3 22 P5 24 (official Gantt). A preempted process keeps the remaining part of its quantum — P1 runs only 1 unit at 4–5 and at 10–11. Resetting the quantum is the common mistake. Avg WT =511+0+12+0+9​=6.4.

Lab 2 Exercises

Lab2-Q1 Counting printed values CH3
pid_t pid = fork();  int cnt = 0;
if (pid == 0) {
    cnt += 10;  pid = fork();
    if (pid != 0) { cnt += 10;  pid = fork(); }
}
printf("%d \n", pid);  printf("%d \n", cnt);

How many non-zero PIDs, how many '0's and how many '10's are printed?

Answer.

4 processes print (pid, cnt): P0 (≠0, 0), C1 (≠0, 20), C2 (0, 10), C3 (0, 20) → 2 non-zero PIDs, 3 zeros, 1 ten. ✔ (verified)

Lab2-Q2 Force the order process 3 → 2 → 1 CH3
int x = 0;
if (BLANK1) { x = x + 1; BLANK2; printf("The value x in process 1 is %d\n", x); }
else if (BLANK3) { x = x + 1; BLANK4; printf("The value x in process 2 is %d\n", x); }
else { x = x + 1; printf("The value x in process 3 is %d\n", x); }

Fill the blanks so the output is always process 3, then 2, then 1 (each printing x = 1).

Answer.

BLANK1 fork() · BLANK2 wait(0) · BLANK3 fork() · BLANK4 wait(0) (fork() > 0 / wait(NULL) also fine). Each process waits for the child it created, so 3 prints before 2, and 2 before 1; every process has its own copy of x, so each prints 1.

Lab 4 Exam Example

Lab4-EX1 Two ordinary pipes for two-way communication CH3

Parent sends "Parent" to the child and the child sends "Child" to the parent using p2c[2] and c2p[2]. Fill BLANK1–BLANK6 (create pipes; child writes then reads; parent reads then writes).

Answer.

BLANK1 pipe(p2c) · BLANK2 pipe(c2p) · BLANK3 write(c2p[1], msg, 6) · BLANK4 read(p2c[0], buffer, 7) · BLANK5 read(c2p[0], buffer, 6) · BLANK6 write(p2c[1], msg, 7) (5 / 6 bytes also accepted). Output: "Parent received the message: Child" and "Child received the message: Parent".

Lab 6 Sample Questions（官方答案）

Lab6-Q1 Semaphores for strict thread order CH6

T1: wait(S1); CS; signal(S2); T2: wait(S2); CS; signal(S3); T3: wait(S3); CS; signal(S1); — initial values for the order T1, T2, T3, T1, …?

Answer.

S1 = 1, S2 = 0, S3 = 0 (only T1 can start; each thread passes the turn to the next).

Lab6-Q2 P0 → P1 → P2 ordering blanks CH6

S0 = BLANK1, S1 = BLANK2, S2 = BLANK3; P0: wait(S0); CS; BLANK4; P1: BLANK5; CS; BLANK6; P2: BLANK7; CS; signal(S0);

Answer.

S0 = 1, S1 = 0, S2 = 0; BLANK4 signal(S1); BLANK5 wait(S1); BLANK6 signal(S2); BLANK7 wait(S2).

Lab6-Q3 Mutex blanks CH6

void *add(void *arg) { pthread_mutex_t* m = BLANK1; for (5000 times) { BLANK2; ++counter; BLANK3; } } — two threads run add with &mutex. Missing code? Purpose? Final counter?

Answer.

BLANK1 (pthread_mutex_t*) arg · BLANK2 pthread_mutex_lock(m) · BLANK3 pthread_mutex_unlock(m). Purpose: protect the shared variable counter (critical section). Final value 10,000.

Lab6-Q4 Possible outputs with semaphores X, Y = 0 CH6

Process A: wait(X); print "b"; signal(Y); wait(Y); print "c"; signal(Y); Process B: signal(X); print "a"; wait(Y); print "d";

Answer.

If both complete: abcd, bacd, bcad. If B takes Y first, A blocks forever at its second wait(Y) → bad, abd (A never finishes). ✔ (verified by exhaustive search)

Lab6-Q5 Counting semaphore permits CH6

S0 = 1, S1 = S2 = S3 = 0. P0: while(true){ wait(S0); print '1'; release(S1); release(S2); release(S3); } P1: wait(S1); release(S0); P2: wait(S2); release(S0); wait(S3); release(S0); — how many '1's?

Answer.

4 — S0 permits: initial 1 + P1 gives 1 + P2 gives 2. After the first print P0 releases S1, S2, S3, so P1 and P2 can produce all of them; then P0 blocks forever. ✔ (verified)

Lab6-Q6 Readers–writers with two mutexes CH6

Fill the reader's blanks (mutex protects read_count; rw_mutex protects the data).

Answer.

Entry: pthread_mutex_lock(&mutex); read_count++; if (read_count == 1) pthread_mutex_lock(&rw_mutex); pthread_mutex_unlock(&mutex); Exit: pthread_mutex_lock(&mutex); read_count--; if (read_count == 0) pthread_mutex_unlock(&rw_mutex); pthread_mutex_unlock(&mutex); The first reader locks writers out and the last reader lets them in.

Lab6-Q7 Race condition values CH6

a = 1, b = 3, c = 0. Thread 1: a = b + 1; c = a - b; Thread 2: a = 13; b = 10; c = 2; All possible final values of c?

Answer.

−6, 1, 2, 3, 10 — 2 if T2's c = 2 is last; 1 (T1 reads a=4, b=3 then T2 runs; or T2 first then a = 11, c = 11 − 10); −6 (T1 reads a=4, then T2 sets b=10); 3 (T2 runs after T1's a = 4, T1 reads a=13, b=10); 10 (T1 reads a=13 and b=3 between T2's writes). ✔ (verified by exhaustive search)

歷屆 MC（S26 / F20 / Sp21 / HW1 / HW2 / Lab 4）

S26-MC1 Interrupts → C

Which of the following statements about interrupts is false?

A. Interrupts may be generated by hardware devices B. Interrupts may be generated by software exceptions or traps C. All interrupts are serviced in exactly the same way, with no difference in priority D. Interrupts are handled by the kernel
interrupt 有 priority levels，high-priority 可以 preempt low-priority interrupt [3.24]。
S26-MC2 DMA → B

Which of the following statements is true about DMA?

A. DMA is used to move data for slow devices, while CPU is used for fast devices B. DMA allows data transfer between device and memory with less CPU involvement C. DMA eliminates interrupts completely D. CPU and DMA can't execute concurrently
DMA 用於 fast devices / large data（A 相反）；完成後仍然 interrupt CPU（C 錯）；CPU 同 DMA 可以 concurrent（D 錯）[3.25]。
S26-MC3 Storage hierarchy → D

Which of the following statements is true about storage hierarchy?

A. Registers are slower than main memory B. Main memory is nonvolatile C. Hard-disk drives are smaller than volatile memory D. Main memory is byte addressable
each address refers to one byte [1.30]。Registers 最快；main memory volatile；HDD 大過 memory。
S26-MC4 von Neumann → B

Which of the following is a core characteristic of the von Neumann architecture?

A. Instructions and data are stored in separate physical memories B. Instructions and data are stored in the same memory space, accessed by address C. The CPU does not contain an ALU; all computations are done by an external co-processor D. The Program Counter (PC) is stored in external mass storage devices
stored-program architecture [1.26]。A 係 Harvard architecture。
S26-MC5 OS services → C

Which of the following is false about services of operating systems?

A. User interface can be CLI or GUI B. The logging service of OS should keep track of computer resources that each user uses C. Errors only occur in memory and I/O devices D. Resource allocation service should allocate resources like CPU cycles, memory, file storage
errors 可以喺 CPU and memory, I/O devices, user programs [2.5]。
S26-MC6 API → A

Which of the following is an advantage of using APIs instead of directly invoking system calls?

A. APIs provide a more convenient programming interface B. APIs always execute faster than system calls C. APIs can bypass kernel protection D. APIs eliminate the need for linkers and loaders
API 好處 = portability + hide complex details（convenient） [2.17]。
S26-MC7 Microkernel → B（C 亦接受）

Which is false about microkernel system structure?

A. It is easier to extend a microkernel operating system B. It typically has better performance than a monolithic kernel C. It runs memory management in user space D. It is easier to port a microkernel operating system to new architectures
microkernel performance suffers（message passing overhead）[2.48]；microkernel 保留 minimal memory management 喺 kernel，所以 C 都算錯。
S26-MC8 printf vs write → B

What's the relationship between printf() and write()?

A. Both printf() and write() are system calls provided directly by the kernel B. printf() invokes write() system call to get service from operating system C. The program enters kernel mode immediately when printf() is called D. write() system call invokes printf() to perform the print function
printf() 係 C library function，佢 call write() system call [2.26]。
S26-MC9 Layered design → B

Which of the following statements about a layered operating-system design is correct?

A. Any layer may directly access any other layer B. The interfaces between adjacent layers are usually well defined C. Layered design eliminates all performance overhead D. Pure layered design is the dominant structure in all modern operating systems
每層只用下層服務、interface well defined（information hiding）[2.44–2.45]。A 係 LKM 特色；layered 有 overhead；好少 pure layered。
S26-MC10 fork count → C
int main() {
   int i;
   for (i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
      if (fork() == 0) {
         fork();
         printf("X ");
         return 1;
      }
   }
   printf("Y ");
   return 0;
}

What is the total number of processes (including the original), the number of "X " printed, and the number of "Y " printed?

A. Total processes = 4, "X " = 3, "Y " = 1 B. Total processes = 4, "X " = 1, "Y " = 3 C. Total processes = 7, "X " = 6, "Y " = 1 D. Total processes = 7, "X " = 1, "Y " = 6
只有 original 繼續 loop；每輪生 1 個 child，child 再 fork → 2 個印 X 然後 return。3 輪 × 2 = 6 X；original 印 1 Y；total = 1 + 6 = 7（已用 C 程式驗證）。

S26-MC23 Mutex + semaphore output → A
int counter = 0; pthread_mutex_t mtx; sem_t sem;   /* sem_init(&sem, 0, 0) */
void *worker1(void *arg) { pthread_mutex_lock(&mtx); counter = counter + 2;
    printf("A %d;", counter); pthread_mutex_unlock(&mtx); sem_post(&sem); return NULL; }
void *worker2(void *arg) { sem_wait(&sem); pthread_mutex_lock(&mtx); counter = counter + 3;
    printf("B %d;", counter); pthread_mutex_unlock(&mtx); return NULL; }
/* main creates t1 (worker1) and t2 (worker2), then joins both */

What is the output?

A. A 2; B 5; B. B 3; A 5; C. A 3; B 5; D. B 2; A 4;

Lab4-MC Threads share memory, processes do not → B
void *child(void *arg) { int *counter = (int *) arg; (*counter)++; return NULL; }
int main() {
    int counter = 0;  pthread_t thread;
    pthread_create(&thread, NULL, child, (void *)&counter);
    pthread_join(thread, NULL);
    printf("%d\n", counter);
    counter = 0;
    pid_t pid = fork();
    if (pid) wait(NULL);
    else { child((void *)&counter); exit(0); }
    printf("%d\n", counter);
}

What is the output?

A. 0 then 0 B. 1 then 0 C. 0 then 1 D. 1 then 1
thread 同 main 共用 counter → 印 1；fork 出嚟嘅 child 改嘅係自己嗰份 copy → parent 印 0。Threads share memory space, processes have separate memory spaces.（Lab 4）

With exponential averaging, if α=0 then:

A. Only the last CPU burst counts B. Recent history does not count; the prediction never changes C. All bursts are weighted equally D. The prediction is always 0
τn+1​=τn​ [5.22]。
P-ch5-5 SJF as priority → B

SJF is a special case of priority scheduling where the priority is:

A. The arrival time B. The inverse of the predicted next CPU burst C. The process ID D. The period of the task
[5.25]。
P-ch5-6 MLFQ preemption rule → C

In the lecture's MLFQ, when a job running from Q1 is preempted by a new arrival in Q0, it:

A. Is demoted to Q2 B. Joins the tail of Q1 with a fresh quantum C. Joins the head of Q1 with its remaining quantum D. Is moved to Q0
[5.31]。
P-ch5-7 Logical CPUs → D

A quad-core processor with 2 hardware threads per core appears to the OS as how many logical processors?

A. 2 B. 4 C. 6 D. 8
4 × 2 = 8 [5.42]。
P-ch5-8 Push migration → B

Push migration means:

A. An idle processor pulls a waiting task from a busy processor B. A specific task periodically checks loads and moves tasks from overloaded to idle/less-busy CPUs C. A process specifies the CPUs it may run on D. A thread is pinned to one core forever
A = pull migration [5.46]；C = hard affinity [5.45]。
P-ch5-9 Affinity system call → A

In Linux, which system call supports hard affinity?

A. sched_setaffinity() B. setpriority() C. clone() D. nice()
[5.45]。
P-ch5-10 RM optimality → B

Rate-monotonic scheduling is optimal in the sense that:

A. It always achieves 100% CPU utilization B. If a task set cannot be scheduled by RM, it cannot be scheduled by any other static-priority algorithm C. It never misses deadlines D. It handles aperiodic tasks best
[5.52]。
P-ch5-11 EDF requirement → C

What is the only requirement EDF places on a process?

A. It must be periodic B. It must have a constant CPU burst C. It must announce its deadline to the scheduler when it becomes runnable D. Its period must be a power of 2
[5.52]。
P-ch5-12 RM utilization → B

Two periodic tasks: P1 (period 50, burst 25), P2 (period 80, burst 35). Under RM:

A. Total utilization is 75% and no deadline is missed B. Total utilization ≈ 94% and P2 misses its deadline at 80 (finishes at 85) C. P1 misses its deadline D. EDF would also miss a deadline
[5.50–5.51]；EDF 可以全部 meet。
P-ch5-13 Deterministic modeling → B

Which statement about deterministic modeling is correct?

A. It uses probability distributions of CPU bursts B. It takes a predetermined workload and gives exact numbers, but results apply only to that workload C. It requires running the real system D. It is the most accurate method
[5.54]。
P-ch5-14 Response time (course definition) → C

RR with q = 4; P1 (24), P2 (3), P3 (3) all arrive at 0 in that order. Using the course definition, the average response time is:

A. 3.67 B. 5.67 C. 7 D. 15.67
end of first run − arrival = 4, 7, 10 → avg 7 [5.13]。（3.67 係課本「first start」定義；5.67 係 avg WT；15.67 係 avg TAT）
P-ch5-15 Non-preemptive kernel / scheduling → B

Scheduling that happens only when a process switches from running to waiting or terminates is called:

A. Preemptive B. Non-preemptive (cooperative) C. Real-time D. Multilevel
[5.6]。
P-ch5-16 SMP common queue issue → A

With a single common ready queue in SMP, what must the system guard against?

A. Two processors choosing to schedule the same thread (race condition) B. Processor affinity being too strong C. Too many push migrations D. Memory stalls
[5.39]。
P-ch6-1 Disabling interrupts → B

Why is disabling interrupts not a good critical-section solution on multiprocessors?

A. It is not allowed in kernel mode B. It is inefficient — interrupts must be disabled on all processors C. It causes race conditions on uniprocessors D. It requires semaphores
[6.13]。
P-ch6-2 CAS return value → C

compare_and_swap(&value, expected, new_value) returns:

A. new_value B. expected C. The original value of *value D. TRUE if the swap happened
[6.17]。
P-ch6-3 Negative semaphore → B

In the blocking (no busy waiting) semaphore implementation, a value of −3 means:

A. The semaphore is broken B. Three processes are waiting on the semaphore C. Three resources are available D. Three signals were lost
[6.26]。
P-ch6-4 Spinlock usage → B

Spinlocks are most appropriate when:

A. Locks are held for a long time on a uniprocessor B. Locks are held for short times on multiprocessor systems C. Processes must sleep while waiting D. Context switches are free
[6.22]。
P-ch6-5 Preemptive kernel → B

Which statement is correct?

A. A preemptive kernel is free from race conditions B. A non-preemptive kernel is essentially free from race conditions in kernel mode (on a single processor) C. Non-preemptive kernels are harder to make correct on SMP than preemptive ones D. Kernel code never has race conditions
[6.12]。
P-ch6-6 Kernel race example → B

The lecture's kernel race-condition example involves two processes calling fork() concurrently. Which variable is at risk?

A. counter B. next_available_pid C. lock D. turn
same PID could be assigned to two processes [6.8]。
P-ch6-7 P and V → B

In Dijkstra's notation, P() and V() correspond to:

A. signal() and wait() B. wait() and signal() C. acquire() and test_and_set() D. lock() and fork()
P = proberen (test)，V = verhogen (increment) [6.24]。
P-ch6-8 Semaphore deadlock → B

P0: wait(S); wait(Q); … P1: wait(Q); wait(S); … with S = Q = 1. What can happen?

A. Starvation only B. Deadlock C. Race condition on S only D. Nothing; this is always safe
[6.28]。
P-ch6-9 Starvation in semaphore queue → A

Starvation (indefinite blocking) can occur with semaphores when:

A. Processes are removed from the waiting queue in LIFO order B. The semaphore is initialized to 1 C. signal() is atomic D. The waiting queue is FIFO
[6.28]。
P-ch6-10 Atomic increment → B

In do { temp = *v; } while (temp != compare_and_swap(v, temp, temp + 1));, why might the loop repeat?

A. Because CAS always fails the first time B. Because another thread changed *v between reading temp and the CAS, so the CAS returned a different value C. Because temp + 1 overflows D. It never repeats
[6.21]。
P-ch6-11 Counting semaphore initial value → C

A counting semaphore controlling access to 5 identical printers should be initialized to:

A. 0 B. 1 C. 5 D. −5
initialized to the number of resources available [6.25]。
P-ch6-12 Simple TAS lock → B

The simple lock while (test_and_set(&lock)); /*CS*/ lock = false; satisfies:

A. Mutual exclusion and bounded waiting B. Mutual exclusion but not bounded waiting C. Bounded waiting but not mutual exclusion D. None of the requirements
要用 waiting[] 版本 [6.19] 先有 bounded waiting。

AC / Pthreads APILab / PA API 速查

Announcement：「There may be questions related to PA or coding questions using some APIs we discussed in our lab classes」→ 呢頁就係用嚟填空 / 寫 code。

1. Process APIs

Call Header Return 重點
pid_t fork(void) <unistd.h> child: 0；parent: child PID (>0)；fail: −1 child 由下一句開始；複製 address space（COW）
int execlp(const char *file, const char *arg0, ..., (char *)NULL) <unistd.h> success: no return；fail: −1 用 PATH 搵 program；arg0 = program name；最後一定要 NULL
int execvp(const char *file, char *const argv[]) <unistd.h> 同上 argv 最後一個元素要係 NULL（PA1：所以 array size 係 9 而唔係 8）
int execl(path, arg0, ..., NULL) / execv(path, argv) <unistd.h> 同上 要 full path（冇 p = 唔搵 PATH）
pid_t wait(int *status) <sys/wait.h> terminated child 嘅 PID；冇 child → −1 wait(NULL) 唔要 status；等任何一個 child
pid_t waitpid(pid_t pid, int *status, int options) <sys/wait.h> 該 child PID；error −1 waitpid(pid, &status, 0) 等指定 child；WNOHANG 唔 block
void exit(int status) <stdlib.h> — 結束 process，status 經 wait 交畀 parent（WEXITSTATUS(status)）
pid_t getpid(void) / getppid(void) <unistd.h> 自己 / parent PID
int chdir(const char *path) <unistd.h> 0 / −1 PA1 cd（唔可以用 exec 做 cd，因為要改 shell 自己嘅 cwd）
sighandler_t signal(int signum, sighandler_t handler) <signal.h> 舊 handler signal(SIGINT, handler)；SIG_IGN 忽略；SIG_DFL default
int kill(pid_t pid, int sig) <signal.h> 0 / −1 send signal to process
unsigned int sleep(unsigned int s) <unistd.h> 剩餘秒數 停 s 秒；usleep = µs；nanosleep（<time.h>）更細

exec family（Lab 3）：六個 — execl, execlp, execle, execv, execvp, execvpe；全部 replace the current process image，成功唔會 return，失敗 −1。

字母 意思 例
l (list) arguments 逐個列出，數目 compile time 已知 execlp("ls", "ls", "-l", "-h", NULL);
v (vector) arguments 放喺 array（尾要 NULL）；數目唔知時用 char *a[] = {"ls", "-l", NULL}; execvp("ls", a);
p (path) 用 PATH 搵 program（唔使 full path） execlp / execvp / execvpe
e (env) 額外傳 environment array execle / execvpe

1.1 經典 fork–exec–wait

pid_t pid = fork();
if (pid < 0) { perror("fork"); exit(1); }
else if (pid == 0) {                       /* child */
    execlp("ls", "ls", "-l", (char *)NULL);
    perror("exec failed");                  /* only reached if exec fails */
    exit(1);
} else {                                   /* parent */
    int status;
    waitpid(pid, &status, 0);              /* or wait(NULL) */
}

1.2 Signal handler（PA1 Feature 2）

void handle_sigint(int signum) {
    printf("Myshell (pid=%d) terminates by Ctrl-C with signal: %d\n", getpid(), signum);
    exit(0);
}
int main() { signal(SIGINT, handle_sigint); /* ... */ }
  • SIGINT = 2（Ctrl-C）；SIGKILL (9)、SIGSTOP 唔可以 catch。

2. File I/O（POSIX，唔係 stdio）

Call Return 重點
int open(const char *path, int flags[, mode_t mode]) <fcntl.h> lowest unused fd / −1 flags：O_RDONLY、O_WRONLY、O_RDWR、O_CREAT、O_TRUNC、O_APPEND；建立檔案要 mode（e.g. 0644）
ssize_t read(int fd, void *buf, size_t count) bytes read；0 = EOF；−1 error blocking（pipe 冇 data 會等；所有 write ends close 晒先 return 0）
ssize_t write(int fd, const void *buf, size_t count) bytes written / −1
int close(int fd) 0 / −1 用完要 close，尤其 pipe write end
int dup(int oldfd) 新 fd = lowest unused close(0); dup(fin); → fd 0 指向 file
int dup2(int oldfd, int newfd) newfd newfd 已開 → 先 close；dup2(fd, 1) = stdout 指向 fd
  • fd 0 = stdin，1 = stdout，2 = stderr（STDIN_FILENO, STDOUT_FILENO, STDERR_FILENO）。
  • Lab 3 permission 寫法：open("hello.txt", O_CREAT | O_WRONLY, S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR)（600：owner read + write）；O_RDONLY 開讀。
  • ⚠️ 唔好用 stdio 嘅 fopen/fread/fwrite/fclose（FILE*）做 PA：FILE* 係 C library struct，cannot be used in pipe operations。
  • Output redirection（cmd > out.txt）：
int fout = open("out.txt", O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, 0644);
dup2(fout, STDOUT_FILENO);  close(fout);   /* then exec */
  • Input redirection（cmd < in.txt）：
int fin = open("in.txt", O_RDONLY);
dup2(fin, STDIN_FILENO);  close(fin);      /* or: close(0); dup(fin); */

3. Pipes

Call 重點
int pipe(int fd[2]) <unistd.h> fd[0] = read end，fd[1] = write end；0 / −1；一定喺 fork() 之前 call
int mkfifo(const char *path, mode_t mode) <sys/stat.h> named pipe（FIFO），之後用 open()/read()/write()；要 unlink() 刪除；0 / −1
int access(const char *path, int how) <unistd.h> F_OK 存在、R_OK/W_OK/X_OK 權限；0 = OK，−1 = 唔得（Lab 4：if (access(FIFO, F_OK) == -1) mkfifo(FIFO, 0777);）
FILE *popen(const char *cmd, const char *type) / int pclose(FILE *fp) <stdio.h> fork 一個 child 跑 cmd；"r" 讀佢 stdout、"w" 寫佢 stdin；pclose 等佢完返回 status（PA1 禁用）
  • FIFO 特性（Lab 4）：open/read/write blocking，要兩端都有 process open 先繼續（可用 O_NONBLOCK）；data 讀咗就冇（唔可以 broadcast）；≤ PIPE_BUF bytes 嘅 write 係 atomic；一條 FIFO 實際唔適合雙向（可能讀返自己寫嘅）→ 雙向用兩條。
  • 兩條 ordinary pipes 做雙向：pipe(p2c); pipe(c2p); → child：close(c2p[0]); write(c2p[1], …); close(p2c[1]); read(p2c[0], …);；parent：close(c2p[1]); read(c2p[0], …); close(p2c[0]); write(p2c[1], …);（Lab 4 exam example）。

3.1 Parent → child

int fd[2]; pipe(fd);
if (fork() == 0) {               /* child: reader */
    close(fd[1]);
    int n; read(fd[0], &n, sizeof(n));
    close(fd[0]); exit(0);
} else {                         /* parent: writer */
    close(fd[0]);
    int n = 6; write(fd[1], &n, sizeof(n));
    close(fd[1]); wait(NULL);
}

3.2 Shell pipeline ls | wc -l

int fd[2]; pipe(fd);
if (fork() == 0) {               /* child 1: ls → pipe */
    dup2(fd[1], STDOUT_FILENO);
    close(fd[0]); close(fd[1]);
    execlp("ls", "ls", (char *)NULL);
}
if (fork() == 0) {               /* child 2: pipe → wc */
    dup2(fd[0], STDIN_FILENO);
    close(fd[0]); close(fd[1]);
    execlp("wc", "wc", "-l", (char *)NULL);
}
close(fd[0]); close(fd[1]);      /* parent MUST close both, else wc never sees EOF */
wait(NULL); wait(NULL);
  • Multi-level pipe（PA1 Feature 5）：n segments → n−1 pipes；segment i：dup2(fds[i-1][0], 0)（if i > 0）、dup2(fds[i][1], 1)（if i < n−1）；每個 child close 所有 pipe fds；parent close 所有 fds 再 wait 全部。

3.3 常見錯誤

  1. pipe() 喺 fork() 之後 call → 兩條唔相關嘅 pipe（HW1 Q3.3c）。
  2. 冇 close 未用嘅 write end → reader read() 永遠唔會得到 EOF（hang）。
  3. write(fd[0], …) / read(fd[1], …) 搞錯方向（0 讀 1 寫：記「0 = stdin-like，1 = stdout-like」）。
  4. read/write 第二個參數要 address（&cnt），第三個係 size（sizeof(int)）。

4. Pthreads（#include <pthread.h>，compile with -pthread）

Call 重點
int pthread_create(pthread_t *tid, const pthread_attr_t *attr, void *(*start)(void *), void *arg) return 0 = success；attr 用 NULL；start routine signature void *f(void *)
int pthread_join(pthread_t tid, void **retval) 等 thread 結束（類似 wait）；retval 可 NULL
void pthread_exit(void *retval) thread 自己結束
int pthread_cancel(pthread_t tid) request cancellation（default deferred）
pthread_t pthread_self(void) 自己 tid
int pthread_kill(pthread_t tid, int sig) signal 指定 thread
int pthread_attr_init(pthread_attr_t *attr) default attributes（stack size, scheduling info）→ 再傳畀 pthread_create（Lab 4 sum example）
pthread_cond_broadcast(&cond) 叫醒所有等緊嘅 threads（pthread_cond_signal 只叫醒一個） 
void *worker(void *arg) { int id = *(int *)arg; printf("thread %d\n", id); return NULL; }
int main() {
    pthread_t t[3]; int id[3];
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) { id[i] = i; pthread_create(&t[i], NULL, worker, &id[i]); }
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) pthread_join(t[i], NULL);
    return 0;
}

4.1 Mutex

pthread_mutex_t m = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;   /* or pthread_mutex_init(&m, NULL) */
pthread_mutex_lock(&m);   /* critical section */   pthread_mutex_unlock(&m);
pthread_mutex_destroy(&m);

4.2 POSIX unnamed semaphore（#include <semaphore.h>）

sem_t s;
sem_init(&s, 0, 1);    /* pshared = 0 → shared between threads of this process; initial value 1 */
sem_wait(&s);          /* P(): if value > 0 decrement, else block */
sem_post(&s);          /* V(): increment, wake a waiter */
sem_destroy(&s);
  • Ordering：sem_init(&s, 0, 0)；先做嘅 thread 做完 sem_post(&s)，後做嘅 thread 開頭 sem_wait(&s)。
  • Mutual exclusion：init 1；sem_wait → CS → sem_post。
  • Counting resources：init = 資源數量 n。

4.3 Condition variables

pthread_mutex_t m; pthread_cond_t c; int ready = 0;
/* waiter */
pthread_mutex_lock(&m);
while (!ready) pthread_cond_wait(&c, &m);   /* releases m while sleeping, re-acquires on wake */
pthread_mutex_unlock(&m);
/* signaller */
pthread_mutex_lock(&m); ready = 1; pthread_cond_signal(&c); pthread_mutex_unlock(&m);
  • 一定要持有 mutex 先 call；用 while（唔係 if）再 check 條件。

5. Compile / Run（Lab 1–2）

gcc -pedantic -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -o myshell myshell.c
gcc prog.c -o prog -lpthread       # pthread programs (or -pthread)
gcc buggy.c -o buggy -g            # debug info, then: gdb buggy
./mlfq < input.txt > output.txt    # PA2: input/output redirection
diff --side-by-side my-out.txt sample-out.txt   # compare outputs (--suppress-common-lines)
gcc main.c -o main -lm             # link math library (linker!)
./prog
  • gcc -c main.c → main.o（compiler）；gcc -o main main.o -lm（linker）；./main（loader）[2.32]。
